title: For Teachers: Clever's Digital Learning Directory
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001712#header1)  
2\. [Viewing and using the Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001712#header2)  
3\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001712#header3)

## Overview

We know many teachers are curious to understand better the digital resources and tools used at their school or district.

If your district or school has enabled it, Clever’s Digital Learning Directory allows you to see a list of all the learning applications your schools are using through Clever.

The Digital Learning Directory provides a list of the applications each school utilizes, which grades use those applications, and an overview of each application with a link to learn more at the application’s website. 

  **![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cIbp&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000N72Pd)  Clever Tip:** Your school or district’s Clever Admin must turn on the Digital Learning Directory. Please contact your IT team if you’d like this feature enabled for your school.

* * *

## Viewing and using the Digital Learning Directory

To view the Digital Learning Directory for your school or district, navigate to the URL your school or district team provided. It will look like this:

**http://clever.com/digital-learning/exampleschoolname**

The Digital Learning Directory will list only learning applications that your district or school has added to the Clever account.

![Example Digital Learning Directory](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cIbp&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000NkUU6)

You’ll be able to filter by school, view an overview of each application, determine which grades are using the application at which schools, and navigate to the application’s web page to learn more.

If your district or school hasn’t enabled or has disabled the directory, you’ll receive the following error:

![Digital Learning Directory disabled](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cIbp&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000NBovV)

Please contact your district or school’s IT team directly with any questions about allowing access to the Digital Learning Directory.  
  
  
 

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Why did I receive a “Digital Learning Directory disabled” page?**

-   Your district or school has disabled or not enabled the Digital Learning Directory. Please contact your district or school’s IT team directly with any questions about allowing access to the Digital Learning Directory.
    

**What if I don’t see a resource that I or my school uses listed?**

-   Only applications added in Clever by your Clever Admin will show in the Digital Learning Directory. If you have questions about the applications your district or school is utilizing, please reach out to your internal team directly.
    

**I see an application that I’d like to start using! Who do I contact?**

-    If you have questions about the applications your district or school is utilizing, please reach out to your internal team directly. The Clever team can’t provide access to your district’s or school’s resources.
    

**I’m using a Clever Library application but I don’t see it in the Digital Learning Directory, why is that?**

-   The Digital Learning Directory will only include applications added by your district or school.
    

* * *

**Related articles:**

-   [For Clever Admins: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001711)
    
-   [For Families: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001713)

title: For Clever Admins: Clever's Digital Learning Directory
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001711#header1)  
2\. [Setting up and viewing your Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001711#header2)  
3\. [Access for families and teachers](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001711#header3)  
4\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001711#header4)

## Overview

We know cybersecurity requirements are rapidly changing, and many states now require school organizations to share which digital resources are used with students openly.

Clever’s Digital Learning Directory generates a website where teachers and families can see all the learning applications your schools are using through Clever with just the click of a button.

The Digital Learning Directory will provide teachers and families with a list of the applications each school is utilizing, which grades those applications are used in, and an overview of each application with a link to learn more at the application’s website.

* * *

## Setting up and viewing your Digital Learning Directory

To activate your Digital Learning Directory, navigate to your [Clever Dashboard > Portal > Portal settings > Digital Learning Directory tab.](https://schools.clever.com/portal/settings/digital-learning-directory)

From here, you can toggle the Digital Learning Directory for your schools on and off. Clever automatically provides a link to your school’s Digital Learning Directory. Currently, this link is not customizable and is determined by the school organization shortname listed in your [Portal URL.](https://schools.clever.com/portal/settings/url)

To preview the Digital Learning Directory for your schools, turn the directory on, then navigate to the provided URL.

![Screenshot of a Digital Learning Directory page](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cScn&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000NkUh0)

Here, you’ll see the Digital Learning Directory that Clever has automatically generated based on the learning applications you have in your Clever account.  The directory will display the following application types:

-   SSO/Rostering
    
-   SSO-only
    
-   Rostering-only
    
-   SSO (Saved Passwords)
    
-   SSO (SAML)
    

  
 

* * *

## Access for families and teachers

You can provide access to the Digital Learning Directory by sharing the URL on your [Portal > Portal settings > Digital Learning Directory tab](https://schools.clever.com/portal/settings/digital-learning-directory). Depending on the group you are sharing the directory with, we also recommend sharing the following articles as well:

-   [For Teachers: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001712)
    
-   [For Families: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001713)
    

If you disable the Digital Learning Directory, users will receive the following error when navigating to the directory in the future:

![Screenshot of the Digital Learning Directory Disabled warning](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cScn&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000NBn6b)    
  
 

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**How should we share this link with families?**

-   We recommend that you include your Digital Learning Directory link in any documentation that you have for families where you want to proactively share these resources with them.
    

**What types of applications will show in the Digital Learning Directory?**

-   SSO/Rostering, SSO-only, rostering-only, SSO (Saved Passwords), and SSO (SAML) applications.
    

**Can we customize our Digital Learning Directory URL?**

-   Not at this time.
    

**What will happen if we don’t have the directory setup but someone tries to navigate to our URL?**

-   They will receive an error page notifying them that your school doesn’t have the directory setup.
    

**Can I print a list of Digital Learning Directory applications?**

-   Not at this time
    

* * *

**Related Articles:**

-   [For Teachers: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001712)
    
-   [For Families: Digital Learning Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001713)

title: For Clever Admins: Syncing administrators via CSV
text:
This article contains the following: 1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001709#header1) 2\. [Creating administrators via CSV](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001709#header2) 3\. [Removing administrators synced via CSV](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001709#header3) 4\. [Viewing and editing team members](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001709#header4) 5\. [Frequently asked questions](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001709#header5) ## Overview Clever's SFTP data syncs allow schools to automate the creation, management, and deletion of administrators. This enhancement brings the same automation to administrative users that Clever already provides for staff, teachers, and students, making the process of provisioning administrator accounts more secure.   **![Pencil icon indicating an important note](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000duwn&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000f4yys)  Please note:** This feature is only available to school organizations utilizing an SFTP sync. If you use a Clever-managed auto sync, you cannot sync administrators via CSV at this time. * * * ## Creating administrators via CSV Administrators include individuals such as central and school office staff who need to manage applications, identities, and users. When creating the administrators.csv, there are three standard admin roles on Clever that can be included: - Clever Administrator - District Help Desk - District Curriculum Lead For an outline of the permissions associated with each role above, please see [this Help Center article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115001733726). You can also create custom administrator roles directly in the Clever Dashboard. Learn more about [custom roles here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001702). If you intend to include custom roles in your administrators.csv, you must first create the role in the Dashboard. All assigned user roles will be displayed on the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) in the **Roles** column. The administrators.csv file provides information about users that you want to have management responsibilities and permissions for your Clever account. The table below outlines the required headers for your administrators.csv.  Headers are case-sensitive. You can view [example CSV files here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1VS6CqRZrMTep8c1_WJjNaHXwMEdHqZSelvunhfnkSL4/template/preview).

Column Header

Required

Format

Notes

Admin_idYesStringAn identifier provided by the school organization when syncing or creating this administrator
Admin_emailYesEmailThe user's email address
First_nameYesStringThe user's first name
Last_nameYesStringThe user's last name
TitleYesStringThe user's title
RoleYesString

User’s administrative role in Clever. Acceptable role values are:

  • Clever Administrator, CleverAdministrator, CA

  • District Curriculum Lead, DistrictCurriculumLead, DCL

  • District Help Desk, DistrictHelpDesk, DHD


Users can also be assigned a custom role. To assign a custom role list the title of the custom role here. The custom role must exist in the Clever Dashboard to be used in the administrators.csv.


If left blank, or containing any unrecognized value across all administrative roles, the administrator role will not be created.

To assign multiple roles to a single administrator, please include a unique row for each role. You’ll need to use the same Admin\_id for each row. Once your administrators.csv is ready to upload, please add this file to your remote SFTP site. As a reminder, you can find the credentials for your remote site on your [Data sources > SIS sync > Settings](https://schools.clever.com/sync/settings) page in the SFTP Settings box. Once you upload the file to the remote site, a data sync will run. The sync may take up to 15 minutes to complete and for the new users to show up in your Clever Dashboard. For guidance on uploading files to your remote CSV site, please see the [Option 2: FTP Client section of our article SFTP Syncs: Uploading data to Clever](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202494408). ![An example of the SFTP Settings box you’ll find on your Sync Settings page](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000duwn&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000pB69a) Any administrator included in the administrators.csv that has an existing administrator account that was manually added in Clever will have their information updated to match the administrators.csv.   **![Pencil icon indicating an important note](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000duwn&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Kulry)  Please note:** Once a user is ‘matched,’ their account is fully managed by administrators.csv. Removing a ‘matched’ user from the administrators.csv will delete their administrator account. If a user has an administrator account today and isn’t included in the administrators.csv, they’ll retain their existing account and permissions. You can continue to manage those users directly on the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members). * * * ## Removing administrators synced via CSV To remove administrators included in the administrators.csv, delete their data from the file and reupload it. For admins added manually via the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members), then later added to the administrators.csv, deleting them from the administrators.csv will also delete their account. For administrators added manually via the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members), their account can be deleted by clicking the trash icon next to their record on the Team page. * * * ## Viewing and editing team members To view any existing team members, navigate to your [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team](https://schools.clever.com/team/members). On the Admin team page, you’ll see an icon next to each user’s name indicating if a colleague manually added them via the Clever Dashboard or if an admin added their account via CSV. Hovering over the icon will provide more information. You can view and edit team members added manually via the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) by clicking the pencil icon. To edit team members added via administrators.csv, please make changes within your administrators.csv and reupload to your remote site. If you're using an SFTP sync, you can also view manually created team members via your [Clever Dashboard > Data sources > Custom data > Admins](https://schools.clever.com/custom-data/browse/admins) tab. If you use a Clever-managed auto sync you won't see the admin tab and will need to edit and view admins via the [Admin team page](https://schools.clever.com/team/members). * * * ## Frequently asked questions **How will I know if the sync created an administrator?** - You'll see new administrators on the [Clever Dashboard > SIS sync > Last Attempted Sync](https://schools.clever.com/sync) page in the Clever Admins column or on your [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) page. Since a data sync must complete, it may take up to 15 minutes for users to appear. **How will administrators be notified that their account was created?** - If the user is having an administrative account created for them, they’ll be sent an email automatically. If the user has an existing administrator account, then they won’t be notified. **Is there a limit to the number of roles a single administrator can hold?** - No, one user can be assigned every role in your Clever account. **What is the user experience for an administrator who holds multiple administrative roles?** - A user who has multiple administrative roles will see every element of Clever assigned to them based on the totality of their permissions. **Can a user be an administrator and a non-administrator role (i.e., Teacher or Staff?)** - Yes. A user can hold multiple user types in Clever. **What if I include a user in the administrators.csv but don't see them on the Last attempted sync page or the Team page?** - There's been an error. Please check the file in the **Download Changes** column on your [Last attempted sync page](https://schools.clever.com/sync) to review any formatting errors. You will need to resolve the errors in your administrators.csv and reupload the file to the remote site. If this doesn’t resolve the issue, please reach out to Clever Support, and we’ll help troubleshoot. **What if I accidentally upload a blank or inaccurate administrators.csv?** - No problem! Please update and reupload your file. If you need assistance, contact Clever Support, and we’ll help you troubleshoot. **What if I attempt to assign an administrator a role that doesn’t currently exist in my Clever account?** - The administrator will not sync to Clever. You must include a role that exists in your Clever account. **I noticed that School Tech Leads are listed on the Team page. Are STLs considered administrators?** - While you can see STLs on the Team page, they are managed through the Staff file, not the Administrators file. Please don’t include anyone in the administrators.csv that shouldn’t have an administrative role. **Will existing administrators be deleted through this process?** - You can delete existing administrators through this process, but only if that is your intention. Here is what you can expect: - If a user has an administrative account today and isn’t included in the administrators.csv, their account won’t be impacted. - If a user has an administrative account today and is included in the administrators.csv, then the synced record will take precedence. - Any user whose account was previously included in the administrators.csv but isn’t present in the next sync will have their account deleted. **Can I still create administrators on the Team page?** - Yes! These accounts will exist separately from any accounts created via your administrators.csv. * * * **Related Articles:** - [For Clever Admins: Managing custom admin roles](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001702) - [Clever Roles: Overview of Roles & Permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115001733726)

title: For App Partners: Getting attendance data from districts
text:
This article contains the following: 1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001705#header1) 2\. [What attendance data is shared with app partners](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001705#header2) 3\. [Learn more about the district experience](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001705#header3) 4\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001705#header5) ## Overview Clever is piloting a new way for districts to send student attendance data to select educational applications.  These apps can use attendance information for many purposes. Here are some use cases with some example students and districts: Here are some examples of how you may use attendance data that’s shared with an app:

Use case

Details

Emergency response & student safetyDuring an unexpected fire drill, the school’s safety system syncs attendance data via Clever’s API. Teachers confirm which students are present, and the system alerts the administration that Alex, a 3rd grader, has not checked in. Staff quickly confirm that Alex was picked up early, preventing unnecessary panic and ensuring an accurate headcount.
Student transportation optimizationEach morning, your district’s transportation system pulls attendance data via Clever’s API. When a student is marked absent, the system removes them from the bus route for that day, reducing unnecessary stops and optimizing fuel efficiency. This helps buses run on time and improves transportation logistics.
Parent communication for absencesLiam’s school uses an app to send automatic alerts when a student is absent. When Liam misses school without a parent excuse, his mother receives a text notification in her preferred language, reminding her to submit a reason. This helps ensure proper documentation and reduces chronic absenteeism.
Absenteeism's impact on learning outcomesDavid, a high school junior, struggles in math and has been absent frequently. The district’s assessment tool is integrated with Clever’s attendance data. Likewise, his teacher notices a correlation between his absences and declining test scores. With this insight, David is given extra tutoring sessions during advisory periods, leading to improved test performance and engagement.
Personalized learning adjustments Sophia, a 5th grader, is using a math app to learn multiplication concepts. Due to frequent absences, she has fallen behind. With Clever’s attendance data integration, the math app’s adaptive learning system identifies gaps in her knowledge and automatically assigns personalized exercises, helping her catch up at her own pace.
If you’re interested in receiving attendance data, keep reading! This article provides a high-level overview of attendance data for application partners. If you’re a district or want to learn more about the district experience, read this article. * * * ## What attendance data is shared with app partners Clever is ingesting, storing, and exposing negative attendance data to application partners. This means any value that is not “Present”, including: - Absent - Tardy - Excuse\_code, if shared by the district: - For example, “ED” for Early Dismissal, or “UA” for unexcused absence. - We currently don't filter any data sent by districts, so data is being stored as-is. Attendance data is stored for up to 6 months from the date it was recorded.  * * * ## How to gain access to attendance data If you’d like access to attendance data, follow these steps: 1. Ensure you are on version 3.1 of the Clever API. 2. Talk to your Application Success Manager within Clever to express your interest. 3. Once the first two steps are done, and a district you’re connected to uploads attendance data, you can make a request to the Clever API with a [district-app token](https://dev.clever.com/docs/api-overview#district-app-tokens) to receive this data.  * * * ## Learn more about the district experience  Check out the [district-facing article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001704) for more information!   * * * ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) **How do districts share the attendance data?** - They share via their existing SFTP box, ensuring compatibility with any SIS. * * * **Related articles:** - [For Clever Admin: Attendance data in Clever](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001704)

title: For Clever Admin: Attendance data in Clever
text:
This article contains the following: 1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001704#header1) 2\. [What attendance data is shared with app partners](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001704#header2) 3\. [Use cases for attendance data](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001704#header3)  4\. [How to add attendance data](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001704#header4) 5\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001704#faq) ## Overview Clever is offering a new way for districts to send student attendance data to select educational applications. This article provides a high-level overview of attendance data in Clever, how it’s added, and other logistical info. * * * ## What attendance data is shared with app partners Any application using Clever for rostering can request access to attendance data through the Clever API at no additional cost to them or you.  Clever will grant access to approved application partners, and schools are always in control of whether or not to share their attendance data. If you’d like to use attendance data with a specific app, please contact the app provider directly to confirm support and request setup. Clever is ingesting, storing, and exposing negative attendance data to application partners. This means any value that is not “Present”, including: - Absent - Tardy - Excuse\_code, if shared by the district: - For example, “ED” for Early Dismissal, or “UA” for unexcused absence. - We currently don't filter any data sent by districts, so data is being stored as-is. Attendance data is stored for up to 6 months from the date it was recorded.   * * * ## Use cases for attendance data  Here are some examples of how you may use attendance data that’s shared with an app:

Use case

Details

Emergency response & student safetyDuring an unexpected fire drill, the school’s safety system syncs attendance data via Clever’s API. Teachers confirm which students are present, and the system alerts the administration that Alex, a 3rd grader, has not checked in. Staff quickly confirm that Alex was picked up early, preventing unnecessary panic and ensuring an accurate headcount.
Student transportation optimizationEach morning, your district’s transportation system pulls attendance data via Clever’s API. When a student is marked absent, the system removes them from the bus route for that day, reducing unnecessary stops and optimizing fuel efficiency. This helps buses run on time and improves transportation logistics.
Parent communication for absencesLiam’s school uses an app to send automatic alerts when a student is absent. When Liam misses school without a parent excuse, his mother receives a text notification in her preferred language, reminding her to submit a reason. This helps ensure proper documentation and reduces chronic absenteeism.
Absenteeism's impact on learning outcomesDavid, a high school junior, struggles in math and has been absent frequently. The district’s assessment tool is integrated with Clever’s attendance data. Likewise, his teacher notices a correlation between his absences and declining test scores. With this insight, David is given extra tutoring sessions during advisory periods, leading to improved test performance and engagement.
Personalized learning adjustments Sophia, a 5th grader, is using a math app to learn multiplication concepts. Due to frequent absences, she has fallen behind. With Clever’s attendance data integration, the math app’s adaptive learning system identifies gaps in her knowledge and automatically assigns personalized exercises, helping her catch up at her own pace.
  * * * ## How to add attendance data You’ll follow these steps to add attendance data once it’s available for one of your applications: 1. **Your district uploads attendance data to Clever** via [your SFTP folder](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202494408?language=en_US#option2) (like how you might upload other CSVs) as an attendance.CSV file. 2. Clever processes the file and makes attendance data available to **approved applications** you're connected to.  1. If you’d like to check if any apps accept attendance data (or you’d like to add them to the approved list for your district), please contact Clever Support by clicking the chat icon in the bottom right. Work through the prompts and submit a ticket. 3. Apps that have been granted **attendance access** by Clever can request this data through our secure API. **![instructor\_c8mlopv788bh4spwj0xrzn2c2\_public\_1712091784\_Lightbulb.1712091783969.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dYkz&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Clever Tip:** For now, there is **no dashboard upload or visibility** for attendance. Clever handles setup and troubleshooting internally.   * * * ## CSV specifications for attendance data You should format your attendance CSV as follows before [sending it to your SFTP box](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202494408?language=en_US#option2). 
Column headerRequiredFormatAvailable via API?Notes
Attendance_idNOStringYES

Unique and constant id for attendance record.

Uniqueness is set at the SIS level and not guaranteed by Clever.

Attendance_dateYESDateYESThe date on which attendance was taken.
Attendance_statusYESOption (enum)YES

Possible values:

*Absent

*Tardy

Excuse_codeNOStringYESAny district code relating to the attendance record.
Student_idYESStringYESUnique and constant id for relevant student. Corresponds to ‘sis_id’ field in Clever. Must be unique across the district.
Section_idNOStringYESIf attendance_type is “section”, the relevant ID of the section. Corresponds to the ‘sis_id’ field on the section object in Clever.
School_idNOStringYESUnique and constant id for the school that the attendance record is assigned to. Corresponds to ‘sis_id’ field in Clever. Must be unique across the district.
Attendance_typeNOOption (enum)YESSupported values: “daily” or “section.” If not available, Clever will calculate based on whether or not there is a corresponding “section_id” on a given record.
* * * ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) **How far back does attendance go?** - Attendance data is stored for up to 6 months from the date it was recorded. **Will attendance data be available no matter what SIS we’re using?** - Yes! Since you’re sharing via your Clever SFTP box, attendance data is available no matter what SIS you’re using!

title: For Clever Admins: Managing custom admin roles
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001702#header1)  
2\. [Creating a custom role](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001702#header2)  
3\. [Assigning the role to a user](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001702#header3)  
4\. [Deleting a role](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001702#header4)  
5\. [Frequently asked questions](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001702#faqs)

## Overview

We know every admin team has a unique structure and needs. Custom admin roles grant specific access in Clever based on your team's unique roles. Custom roles minimize risk by ensuring users have the minimum access required in Clever. 

For example, you may have a curriculum coordinator who only needs access to analytics and the Clever Portal for a few specific schools. Or, you might have a SIS admin who only needs access to Clever’s sync settings. Custom roles offer you endless options for customization to ensure least-privileged access for your admins.

This article will guide you through creating, assigning, and deleting a custom role. For details on the granular permissions available, [please see our article here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756).

## 

* * *

## Creating a custom role

When creating a custom role, you’ll want to consider the permissions the user should have. We recommend reviewing all of our [granular permission options here.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756)

Additionally, Custom roles can have permissions at all schools in a school organization or only specific schools. When creating your custom role, if you wish to assign specific schools, you’ll currently only have the option to allow this role to access certain permissions in the Support Tools, Analytics, Portal Management, and SSO + Login management categories as outlined in our [granular permissions article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756).

To get started creating a custom role:

1.  Navigate to your [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team.](https://schools.clever.com/team/members)
2.  Click **Actions > Create custom role.**

![Screenshot of Actions drop down highlighting Create custom role.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IQIBp)

3.  Name your role and add a description. If your new role requires access to specific schools, click **Specific Schools**, then select the schools from the dropdown menu.    
    For this example, we're creating a role for a curriculum coordinator with access to all schools. Role names must be unique (for example, you can’t have two roles named “Math Curriculum Coordinator, but you **can** assign multiple people to the same role). 
    

## ![Screenshot of Role info settings](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000doG6M)

 **![pencil.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** While custom roles allow school-specific scoping within the Clever Dashboard, integrated application partners may receive admin data at the school organization level. If a school-scoped admin is shared with an application, the application may grant the school-scoped admin school organization-wide visibility. To maintain strict data least-privilege, we recommend reviewing which administrative users are shared with apps. 

4.  Decide which permissions users with this role will need. We recommend reviewing the [list of granular permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756) to understand each set of permissions as you create your custom role. Custom roles scoped to specific schools will only include specific permissions in Support Tools, Analytics, Portal Management, and Clever groups.
    
    In this case, the curriculum coordinator needs access to view Clever analytics. However, we don't want them to manage these settings.
    

![Screenshot of Analytics settings](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IQCHj)   
  

5.  They also need access to our **Portal** to add and remove resources.
    

![Screenshot of Portal management settings](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IQLT4)

6.  Once you're satisfied with the permissions, click **Proceed to review**.
    
7.  Review your new role and the permissions and then click **Create role**.

* * *

## Assigning the role to a user

**Assigning a user to the role immediately after creating a role**

1\. If there's a user you want to assign the role to immediately, you can do so right after you’ve created the role. This step is optional.

2\. Click **Assign**.

![Screenshot of Assigning a role](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IQUrK)

**Assigning a user to a role after it’s created**

If you’d like to assign a user to a role after it’s created, head to your [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) **> find the role > Actions > Assign**.

![Screenshot of the Assign user role button](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IQVlm)    
 

You can also add administrators via CSV and assign existing roles in bulk. [Please see this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001709) for more information.

If you want to review an admin’s role, take a look at the [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) page or search for the admin in the search bar, navigate to their profile page, and view it to learn more about their role.

![An admin’s profile page in Clever](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dg7R&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000nDJv6)

* * *

## Deleting a role

If you no longer want a custom role, you can delete it by going to your [Clever Dashboard > User management > Admin team](https://schools.clever.com/team/members) **> find the role > Actions > Delete**.

If there are any users assigned to the role, you must first remove them. After removing any members, you’ll be able to delete the custom role.

* * *

## Frequently asked questions

**Where can I view a list of all permissions available for custom roles?**

-   View a complete list of custom roles permissions [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756).

**Can I assign a role to a user later?**

-   Yes, assigning a role to a user immediately after creating it is optional. You can assign the role at any time.

**Can I change the permissions of a role after creating it?**

-   Yes, you can adjust the permissions of a role after it has been created. These changes will apply to all users who have been assigned the role.

**Can a user have multiple roles?**

-   Yes, a user can be assigned multiple roles, each with its own set of permissions. When a user has more than one admin role, they’ll be granted all permissions associated with both roles.

**Will I still be able to use [standard roles](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115001733726) (such as School Organization Help Desk or School Organization Curriculum Lead)?**

-   Yes, those roles will remain available.

**What will a user see if they attempt to edit sharing for an application they don’t have permission to manage?**

-   If a user attempts to change sharing permissions for an application they don’t have permissions to manage, they’ll receive an **Access restricted** notification that guides them to reach out to a Clever Admin for assistance.

**What custom role permissions are currently available to school-scoped custom admin roles?**

-   See our article [For Clever Admins: Custom role granular permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756) for a list of school-scoped permissions.

* * *

**Related articles:**

-   [Clever Roles: Overview of Roles & Permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115001733726)
-   [For Clever Admins: Syncing administrators via CSV](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001709)
-   [For Clever Admins: Custom role granular permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001756)

title: For Clever Admins: Clever Complete Overview
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001701#header1)  
2\. [Features](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001701#header2)  
3\. [What does this mean for you?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001701#header3)  
4\. [Learn more](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001701#header4)   
5\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001701#header5)

## Overview

Clever Complete is the platform solution purpose-built for edtech scalability, connecting applications to any school through a single, secure integration for rostering, SSO, and LMS connections.

If you currently use Clever, nothing will change in your Clever experience. Clever Complete is a platform solution for application partners to simplify school organization data management into one system: Clever.

If you do not currently utilize Clever, application partners you work with may utilize Clever Complete to more easily synchronize data from your schools. As always, your student data privacy is a top priority for Clever. Learn more about our practices, FERPA, COPPA, GDPR, and state-level compliance in [our Trust Center](https://www.clever.com/trust).

Whether you currently use Clever or not, you’ll be able to continue managing your data via your existing systems while experiencing the benefits of simplified integrations with your application partners.  
 

* * *

## Features

Clever Complete utilizes Clever’s existing 1EdTech OneRoster® integrations to help applications more smoothly integrate with schools without requiring schools to learn any additional systems. Applications using Clever Complete will be able to more easily integrate with your school because they’ll have access to:

-   A single integration point for rostering, SSO, and your LMS
    
-   Additional data fields related to demographics and attendance
    
-   Best-in-class data visibility and management
    

* * *

## What does this mean for you?

If you’re currently using Clever, nothing will change! You’re going to continue getting all of the great benefits of Clever that you always have.

If you’re not currently using Clever, and one or more of your applications utilizes Clever Complete, Clever will serve as a subprocessor of your data. This means that Clever will serve as a middleman between any system you use to send data to your applications, and the application itself.  This will improve your implementation experience with applications as data is normalized and simplified via Clever for application partners to ingest.

Clever is committed to student data privacy and security, complying with COPPA, FERPA, GDPR guidelines. Learn more about our data privacy and security practices [here](https://www.clever.com/trust).

Whether you currently utilize Clever or not, when you use an edtech vendor that leverages Clever Complete you’ll benefit from:

-   Easier onboarding and faster implementation timelines for new edtech tools
    
-   Improved cybersecurity
    
-   Higher quality application integrations and improved troubleshooting
    

* * *

## Learn more

If you’re interested in learning more about how applications will utilize Clever Complete, please check out our article [For Application Partners: Clever Complete Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001700).  
 

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**If I already roster my application via another service, and the vendor wants me to begin rostering via Clever Complete, will I need to take action?**

-   Yes, the Clever team will help you configure your data flow to route through Clever Complete instead of your current provider.
    

**Will Clever Complete impact how my users log in to an application?**

-   No. Schools and applications can continue using their preferred authentication methods while ensuring a seamless login experience for students and educators.
    

**We don’t currently use Clever, how will Clever Complete impact our current environment?**

-   You do not need to utilize Clever for an application partner to utilize Clever Complete to synchronize data from your schools. You can continue managing your data via your existing systems.
    

**Can I choose how I want to roster within Clever?**

-   Yes, school organizations can decide how they want to roster, whether using Clever Secure Sync, OneRoster, or other supported methods. Clever Complete ensures that no matter how a school chooses to roster, applications receive the data they need.
    

* * *

  
 **Related Articles:  
**

-   [For Application Partners: Clever Complete Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001700)

title: For Clever Admins: Clever Badges and cybersecurity
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#header1)  
2\. [Security review: Threat modeling](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#header2)  
3\. [Behind Badge security: Technical specifications](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#header3)  
4\. [Clever Badges versus standard credentials: How Badges help security in schools](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#header4)  
5\. [Security recommendations for Badges](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#header5)  
6. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQS)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001699#FAQs)

## Overview

We know that cybersecurity and digital citizenship are leading priorities for schools. At Clever, we want to partner with you in securing all of your users’ digital identities and providing a seamless authentication experience.

Clever Badges are well known for simplifying student logins, and our teams have taken measures to ensure simple is still secure.

![Image of logging in with a Clever Badge.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cSJR&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IIgUf)

This article outlines the measures we take to build products that are secure by default in our product development process, the safeguards in place for our Clever Badges system, ongoing steps to maintain security across our platform, and recommendations to help you maintain security when implementing Clever Badges with your users.

As always, we recommend evaluating your current cybersecurity practices, environment, and risk tolerance when making decisions for your school regarding authentication and digital identity management.   
 

* * *

## Security review: Threat modeling

Threat modeling is a structured process for identifying security risks in a system. With threat modeling, a team considers what a product will do, who will use it, and what may go wrong. Clever uses threat modeling when developing our products, specifically keeping in mind that many of our end users are students and teachers.

For Clever Badges, this means that our teams continue to analyze the various types of Badges, how they’ll be used for logins, and the users utilizing them. For example, a student can use a Clever Badge to authenticate into just the Clever Portal, or an administrator may configure additional settings so that the student can use their Badge to log into a Chromebook _and_ the Clever Portal.

Alternatively, students or teachers can use Classroom Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) Badges as a second authentication factor to log into Clever or a device. There are a number of ways to utilize Clever Badges, and our team has worked to consider all use cases during threat modeling.

To add an additional level of security, Clever runs a [bug bounty program](https://www.clever.com/trust/security), and any researchers who report a security vulnerability in Clever Badges will receive a cash payout. We also perform code reviews and audits for all security-sensitive feature changes.

Check out our Security recommendations section below to learn more about how our team has considered Badges security across various use cases and settings. 

* * *

## Behind Badge security: Technical specifications

 Clever Badges are QR codes that encode four pieces of data:

1.  a unique identifier that maps to the student
    
2.  a version number for the badge
    
3.  a sequence number that increments each time a new badge is created (login Badges only)
    
4.  a token consisting of 12 bytes of entropy
    

Think of the unique identifier as a ‘username’ and the token as a ‘password.’ Together, they log the user in. The token is the security mechanism that prevents an attacker from guessing the QR code.

Due to the complexity of the token, forging a Clever Badge is extremely difficult. 12 bytes of entropy means that, on average, you’d need 2^(12\*8)/2 attempts to guess the token in a Clever Badge – approximately 40 octillion attempts. Even if someone made one million guesses per second (which we would detect in our logs and actively block) it would take over a quadrillion years to guess. A Clever Badge is approximately as secure as a random 15-character alphanumeric password with symbols.

A cryptographically secure random number generation algorithm is used to generate the token. The token is stored on our servers as a SHA256 hash, which helps mitigate timing attacks.

Using client-side Javascript to parse the values from the QR code image from the web camera, data is transferred for logins to the server side over a TLS-encrypted connection, where they are validated. No video data is sent to our servers. 

On the server, the validation process first validates that the data is well-formatted, looks up the record associated with the student's unique identifier and sequence number, and verifies that the token matches using SHA256. If all elements are confirmed, Clever sets a cookie on the user’s browser, allowing it to use OAuth 2.0 to sign in to other applications.

  
 

* * *

## Clever Badges versus standard credentials: How Badges improve security in schools

PreK-12 school organizations have a wide range of users with an even wider range of technical competencies. For the youngest learners and those with special needs, physically typing in and remembering complex passwords presents a very real challenge when accessing digital education resources.

To mitigate these login difficulties, many teachers and administrators resort to solutions like writing usernames and passwords on post-its, creating simple passwords (i.e., 12345), or using the same username and password for an entire class. These solutions create security gaps that range from other students and teachers stealing login credentials to bad actors easily guessing simple passwords and gaining access to a user’s account.

With a Clever Badge, the primary security gap is if the physical Badge is stolen. For young students, the threat of an insecure username and password is much greater than that of a physical Badge. Simply put, Clever Badges have a ‘physical access’ attack surface that is similar to that of passwords printed and distributed by teachers, but they are more resistant to brute forcing or password guessing. Clever doesn’t offer Badges for teachers because the most secure method for a teacher to log in is a complex username and password; however this same complexity of login is not accessible to a young student.

Clever requires a PIN code for students in seventh grade and above. Additionally, schools can add a PIN code to their Badge settings for students below seventh grade.  
 

* * *

## Security recommendations for Badges

### **Clever Badges**

-   For security reasons, Clever Badges can only be utilized by students. Teachers should log in with a secure username and password.
    
-   Clever recommends that you void and reprint badges during your annual rollover period, such as the summer or winter. 
    
-   Clever requires students in grades seven and above to use a PIN code with their Badge (with exceptions for students with an IEP or ELL status) to provide an additional layer of security.
    
-   Teachers can also bulk print Clever Badges for their students which helps reduce the steps for Badge distribution. They can void Badges as well. We recommend sharing our article [For Teachers: Clever Badges for students](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000127406) with your teachers so they can familiarize themselves with Badge management options to minimize risk if a student’s Badge is lost.
    
-   Just like passwords, Clever Badges are considered sensitive login information. **Never** share Badges via an insecure medium such as email. Badges should be physically handed to the user.
    

### **Classroom MFA Badges**

Multi-factor authentication includes three categories: something you know, something you have, or something you are. When configuring MFA, each method should come from a different category. For example, if you log into your bank account with a username and password and a fingerprint reader, you are logging in with something you know and something you are.

-   Students shouldn’t use a Clever login Badge and a Classroom MFA Badge as both factors when using multi-factor authentication. This login would combine two items you have, which is not the best practice for MFA.
    
    -   For students who use a Clever login Badge as their primary method for logging in, we recommend [picture logins](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001625#selectmethods) as a second factor.
        
-   For security reasons, only student MFA Badges can be bulk printed by Clever Admins, not teacher MFA Badges.
    
-   Teachers can help manage MFA Badges by voiding or generating them in their Portal. We recommend sharing our article [For Teachers: Helping your students set up and troubleshoot Classroom MFA](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001656) with your teachers so they can familiarize themselves with Badge management options to minimize risk if a student’s MFA Badge is lost.
    
-   Just like passwords, Classroom MFA Badges are considered sensitive login information. **Never** share Badges via an insecure medium such as email. Badges should be physically handed to the user.
    

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**How do I know if Clever Badges are the right login method for my school?**

-   We recommend that you consider the current level of risk at your school regarding student logins. If your student usernames and passwords are currently written down, easily guessable, or reused across various students, using a Clever Badge for logins is a more secure option, as the only way to misuse a Badge is by physically obtaining it.

**Can Badges be assigned to work only on specific devices (e.g., in a one-to-one Chromebook environment)?**

-   A Clever Badge being scannable by only a specific device is not possible. The ability to sign into a Chromebook using a Clever Badge can be assigned to specific OUs of users and/or devices where Clever's settings have been configured.

**Can a Badge be forged?** 

-   Technically, it is possible, but it would be extremely difficult! Part of the data encoded by each Badge is a 12-byte token, generated using a cryptographically secure random number generation algorithm, making brute-force guessing unfeasible.

**What happens when a Badge is stolen or lost?  
**

-   Teachers, School Tech Leads, and administrators can void Badges using their Clever accounts. When a Badge is voided, the record is regenerated in the database and the old badge can no longer be used to log in. Clever uses the sequence number in the Badge to track Badges from generation to usage, to help clarify situations where badges have been improperly used.

* * *

**Related Articles:**

-   [Clever Badges: Overview and setup](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/220213907)
    
-   [For Clever Admins: Classroom MFA Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001616)
    
-   [For Teachers: Clever Badges for students](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000127406)
    
-   [For Teachers: Helping your students set up and troubleshoot Classroom MFA](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001656)

title: For Clever Admin: Access logs
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001698#header1)  
2\. [Features of access logs](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001698#header2)  
3\. [How to use Access logs with login error messages from end users](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001698#header3)  
4\. [Frequently asked questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001698#header4)

## Overview

Access logs give you a holistic snapshot of any attempts to access Clever. Use Access logs to spot any suspicious activity early, to keep your schools’ users and data safe. You can also use Access logs to troubleshoot users who are having trouble accessing Clever.

![Screenshot of Access logs](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000VpL0X)

For example, you might notice that a user’s login keeps getting stuck on an MFA timeout, meaning the user has entered their password correctly, but that they are not completing their MFA security method. That could mean that their password has been compromised, and that they need a reset. 

This article covers each feature of access logs and how you might use them.

* * *

## Features of access logs

**Filter functionality**

You can quickly filter access logs by date, IP Address, status, user, and user type. For instance, if you believe a certain user’s account has been compromised, you can drill down to that user to see their access history. In addition, you can look via reference ID (such as an error code a user has shared with you).

![Screenshot of Access logs filter functionality](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC3z3)    
  

**User access activity**

All users (students, teachers, [short-term substitute teachers](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001675), staff, and Clever Admin) access activity shows up as a summary: 

![Screenshot of Access logs user access activity](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000K9cKH)

**Individual access log summary**

If you click the down arrow, you can see useful information, including:

-   the authentication method (e.g. Substitute Badge, MFA, etc.)
-   the final user action
    
-   their user ID
    
-   email address
    
-   error code(s) if relevant
    

![Screenshot of individual access log summary](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC4S5)

Access logs will also include details on Clever Admin and School Tech Lead (STL) impersonations. The authentication method listed will indicate impersonation, and the log summary will contain details such as the impersonation’s start and end time, the user account impersonated into, device details, etc.

![Screenshot of an example of an impersonation event in Access Logs](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Pw6WT)

_An example of an impersonation event in Access logs_

**Emailing CSV exports**

Exports are available only as downloads and will be emailed to the admin who exports them from the Clever Dashboard. You can also email a CSV export by day, which includes all access log data organized by column. If you want to send these exports to a security management solution, you’ll need to send them manually.

![Screenshot of Access logs CSV export](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC4qH)

To pull an export:

1.  Click **Export** **CSV**
2.  Select your dates. You can export data for up to seven days at a time, up to 60 days in the past. If you need more than 7 days of data, you can export the data for multiple 7-day timeframes.
3.  Click **Export CSV:**

![Screenshot of Export CSV modal](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000JzEG1)

**CSV exports include:**

-   Timestamp
    
    -   When the event took place
        
-   Authentication\_context\_id
    
    -   This ID relates to a single user’s single login attempt. For instance, if a user logged in with a primary method, requested an MFA code, had an MFA timeout, and then successfully entered an MFA prompt, these would all be under the same Authentication\_context\_id.
        
-   User\_id
    
    -   The user’s Clever ID
        
-   User\_type
    
    -   Teacher, student, staff, or Clever Admin
        
-   Client\_ip
    
    -   The user’s IP address
        
-   Auth\_method
    
    -   Their primary authentication method, such as SIS, Google, or Clever Passwords.
        
-   Second\_factor
    
    -   Their MFA method (such as Mobile app MFA, SMS code, etc.)
        
-   Event
    
    -   Part of the login process, such as:
        
        -   Login\_success
            
            -   Part of the login process was successful (such as a first method, second method, or backup login code). 
                
        -   Login\_failure
            
            -   Part of the login process was unsuccessful.
                
        -   MFA\_prompted
            
            -   The user was prompted to enter an MFA prompt
                
-   Error
    
    -   There was an issue with the login process, such as a duplicate ID, no match to a user in your schools, etc.
        

* * *

## How to use Access logs with login error messages from end users

When students or teachers can’t log in to Clever, they’ll receive an error message that provides information about the error, a copyable Reference ID, possible troubleshooting steps, and instructions to contact their school’s IT support.

![Screenshot of an example error message an end user may receive when their login fails](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000O79S9)

While the login error may suggest steps towards resolution, if you need additional information, please navigate to your  [Clever Dashboard > Access logs](https://schools.clever.com/access-logs) and input the Reference ID for more details.

If you’re still unsure how to resolve the issue, please [contact Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326) and provide the user’s Clever ID and the Reference ID so our team can help troubleshoot further. 

* * *

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

-   **What’s the length of logging shown in Clever?** 
    
    -   Five days.
        

-   **What’s the length of logging shown from the CSV download?**
    
    -   You can download up to seven days of data from the past 60 days.  
          
        

-   **What does it mean if an authentication method is “Impersonation?”**
    
    -   This means that a Clever Admin impersonated a teacher or student account, or if this setting is enabled for your school, an STL impersonated into a teacher account. Click the Access log entry for more details on the impersonation.
        

-   **What fields can you search via?**
    
    -   As of now, you can only search via reference ID.
        

-   **What errors might we see in a log?**
    
    -   Wrong email, wrong pw, incorrect 2nd factor
        
    -   Pending MFA: users have 10 minutes to complete their MFA challenge, if nothing happens, Clever will fail the login. 
        
    -   Timeout error: Meaning it took longer than 15 seconds for Clever to download your data.
        

-   **What are the differences between our classic login logs versus new access logs?**
    
    -   Length of logs shown:
        
        -   2,000 logs or 14 days in login logs
            
        -   5 days for access logs with no limit on # of logs
            
    -   Download limits:
        
        -   5k logs for login logs
            
        -   14 days with access logs (you can also request a longer history by contacting Clever Support).
            
    -   Access logs also include:
        
        -   Combined logs into one view when there are multiple access touch points, so it’s easier to troubleshoot.
            
        -   More detail around methods of authentication, such as MFA, Substitute Badge access, etc.
            
        -   Better error messaging with more detail on access errors.

title: For Teachers & Students: Claiming your Clever account
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001696#header1)  
2\. [How to Claim your account](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001696#header2)  
3\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001696#header3)

## Overview

If you’re new to Clever, your IT team may share directions for you to claim your Clever account. This article explains how to claim and set up your account. 

IMPORTANT These directions only apply to you if your IT team has set up account claiming in Clever. If you have questions about how to access your Clever account, please contact your IT team. Clever’s Customer Support team can’t help with accounts for students, teachers, and staff since those accounts are managed by your IT team, not Clever.  

* * *

## How to Claim your account

### **Step 1: Get to the account claim page**

#### **Option 1:** If your IT team has sent you a link to claim your account, please click that link. 

#### **Option 2:** Otherwise, go to your [Clever Portal login page](https://clever.com/oauth/district-picker) and click **get help logging in.** 

  
![Screenshot of Clever log in page.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPSUX)   

Then, click **Claim your account.**

![Screenshot of Clever Login Help.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPL6U)

### **Step 2:**

Complete the account claim steps. These will vary based on how your school’s IT team has set it up.

You’ll be asked to submit information such as your account number, email address, and grade. This is to prove you’re really you, and not someone trying to access your account. 

You have a limited number of attempts to claim your account, so please be careful to type your information in correctly. Fields other than email are case sensitive, so please keep this in mind when inputting answers.

![Screenshot of Claim account screen in Clever asking for student ID.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPSpV)

_In this example, the student is first asked for their email address._

![Screenshot of Claim account screen in Clever asking for grade.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPT2P)

_Then, they’re asked for their grade._

### **Step 3: Setting up your account**

Next, you’ll set up your Clever password and get your username. This will look different based on how your IT team has set it up.

#### **Option 1:**

If you see a screen like the one below, you’ll set your password yourself. Type your password twice, then click **Save**.

![Screenshot of Reset Password screen in Clever.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPTTp)

Then, you’ll be shown your Username for Google, Active Directory, and/or Entra ID. Be sure to remember your username and password so you can log in to Clever!

![Screenshot of Your account usernames screen in Clever.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPTiL)

#### **Option 2:**

If you’re shown your username for Google, Active Directory, and/or Entra ID first, your IT team has already set a password for you.

Be sure to remember your username so you can log in to Clever!

![Screenshot of Your account usernames screen in Clever.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPU6X)

Next, you’ll be shown your password. Click the **Show** button to see your password. Then type it twice to make sure you can remember it. When you’re done, click **Go to login**.

![Screenshot of Your accounts password screen in Clever.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bekr&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000GPUL3)   

### **Step 4: Log in to Clever**

You’re all set! After seeing your username and password, you’re ready to log in to Clever.

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**I’m having trouble setting up my account, who do I contact?**

-   Please contact your IT team for help. They manage your account. Clever Support can’t help with account creation or claiming.  
     

Related articles:

-   [For Students: Troubleshooting - Logging in to Clever](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115002717307)
-   [For Teachers: Troubleshooting - Student logins](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/222933888)
-   [For Teachers: Troubleshooting - Teacher logins](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360039685112)
