title: For Clever Admins: Clever Library privacy
text:
**![](https://theme.zdassets.com/theme_assets/364037/af574183f2df705f2c75ac31fc7ab01b1a5a3d9a.png)**For the most comprehensive information about how data is handled for Library applications, please review [Clever’s Universal Data Sharing Agreement (DSA)](https://clever.com/trust/universal-dsa).

##   
Overview

The [Clever Library](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360015683471) lets teachers install applications for themselves and their students, write reviews, and share apps with other teachers.

This article outlines information on the data provided to Library applications via Clever. For more information on Library settings and access, [please see this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360015683471).  
 

* * *

## What data do Clever Library Apps receive?

Clever Library applications added by teachers receive a limited amount of data. These applications do not receive all fields like Secure Sync applications. Find the data Library apps receive for each record type below:

### Teachers

-   Clever ID
-   Name
-   Email

### Students

-   Clever ID
-   Name (first name, last initial)
-   Grade

### Sections

-   Clever ID
-   Name
-   Subject
-   Grade
-   Section number
-   Teachers
-   Students

title: For Teachers: Making a purchase request in Clever Library
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001451#What%20is%20the%20Clever%20Library?)  
2\. [How do I make a purchase request?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001451#How%20do%20I%20make%20a%20purchase%20request?)  
3\. [What happens after a purchase request is made?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001451#What%20happens%20after%20a%20purchase%20request%20is%20made?)

## Overview

The [Clever Library](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360013488672) is a place for teachers to discover, learn about, and adopt new resources for their classrooms. Teachers can browse applications across multiple subjects and grades. Clever also surfaces popular apps in your school organization and across Clever, as well as apps new to the Library. Resources in the Library are added to a teacher’s Teacher Page for easy access by students and teachers.

If you don’t see a Library tab in your Clever Portal, your Clever Admin has disabled the Library. [Learn more here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360013488672?#header6).

* * *

## How do I make a purchase request?

 **![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cPlN&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** In order to make a purchase request, the desired application must first be added to your Teacher Page from the Clever Library. Not all Library apps are available for purchase (such as free apps).

  
In order to add an application from the Clever Library, follow these steps:

1.  Navigate to the **Library** page in your Clever Portal. Find this option in the upper right corner. If you know the name of the application, you can use the search bar. 
    
2.  Click on the desired application and you’ll be taken to the application page. If you don’t see an application, it may not be available in the Library.
    
3.  From the application page, click **Install**. If the **Install** button is gray and not clickable, your Clever Admin has blocked this application. [Learn more here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360013488672?#header6) or contact your admin or IT team for more information.
    
4.  Complete the form on the following page. You can choose which Teacher Pages to display the application on.
    
5.  Click **Allow and continue**.
    

Once an application has been added to your Teacher Page via the Clever Library, you have the ability to request that your school organization purchase the resource. There are two ways to make a purchase request:  
 

### Option 1

1.  Select the application you want to request a purchase for from the appropriate Teacher Page in Clever Portal.
2.  Choose the **Upgrade** option below the application icon.
3.  Fill out the form presented and click **Send Request**.

### Option 2

1.  In the Clever Portal, search for the application by name using the search bar in the upper right corner.
2.  Once the application appears in the dropdown menu, click the link labeled **Details**. This will take you to the application page in the Clever Library.
3.  Click **Request an upgrade**.
4.  Fill out the form presented and click **Send Request**.

* * *

## What happens after a purchase request is made?

Once you’ve submitted your purchase request, Clever Admins and School Tech Leads at your school organization will be notified. Those individuals will determine if they will take action on your purchase request. If you have questions, please reach out to your IT or tech support team.

title: For App Partners: Clever Library
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001450#header1)  
2\. [How does the Clever Library work?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001450#header2)  
3\. [Understanding Teacher Sign-Ups with the Clever Library](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001450#header3)  
4\. [How "Sign Up with Clever" works for teachers](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001450#header4)  
5\. [How "Sign Up with Clever" works for students](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001450#header5)

 **![pencil.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dhuj&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** After reviewing our Library application process, we’ve decided to pause acceptance of new applications for Clever Library certification at this time. If you have any questions, please reach out to [application-interest@clever.com](mailto:application-interest@clever.com). 

## Overview

The [Clever Library](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360013488672) is a place for teachers to discover, learn about, and adopt new resources for their classroom. Resources in the Library can be added to a teacher’s Teacher Page for easy access by students and teachers. 

![Clever Library in Clever with various free and freemium apps](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dhuj&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000VoNdt)

* * *

## How does the Clever Library work?

When a teacher adopts a Library application with SSO, Clever shares only the absolute minimum information: student first name, last initial, grade level, and course enrollment. **Clever does not share any sensitive information with Library applications, including student email, student number, SIS ID, state ID, school/district information, or any demographic information about the student.**

In the Clever Library, teachers can:

-   Add applications for themselves and their students
    
-   Review applications for other teachers to see
    
-   Recommend and share applications to other teachers
    

   **![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dhuj&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000VoNpB)   Please note:** The Clever Admin for each school organization can turn off the Clever Library and block individual resources that they don’t want teachers to access. [Please see this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360015683471) for more information on district and school controls over Library applications.

* * *

## Understanding Teacher Sign-Ups with the Clever Library

**Sign Up with Clever** enables teachers to create accounts for themselves and their assigned students in your application using data from their existing Clever accounts. This streamlines onboarding by automatically setting up accounts without manual data entry. Applications added by teachers through Clever also appear as SSO resources in the Clever Portal for both teachers and their students. 

Currently, only existing teachers in a Clever district can use Sign Up with Clever when utilizing their Clever Library; new teachers who attempt to Sign Up with Clever are directed to have their district IT administrators set up an account with Clever.

Teacher sign-ups with the Clever Library differ from district connections primarily in management and data access. With teacher sign-ups, individual teachers independently decide to connect your application via the Clever Library and can add or remove access at any time. In contrast, district connections are authorized and managed by district-level Clever Admins, who control [Sharing Permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/236233907?language=en_US) to grant access en masse. Teacher sign-ups provide only essential data—teacher and student names, emails, sections taught, and Clever IDs—while district connections share the full [Clever Data Model](https://dev.clever.com/docs/data-model) and support overnight data syncing. Please note that data from teacher sign-ups can only be accessed on login; unlike district connections, teacher sign-ups do not support overnight data syncing.

Click **Analytics** on the left sidebar of your app dashboard to see the total number of students and teachers who are using your application. You can use the “Source” filter to identify the usage coming from teacher sign-ups, district connections, or both.  
 

* * *

## How "Sign Up with Clever" works for teachers

If your application supports Sign Up with Clever, teachers can create an account in your product either via a Login with Clever button on your website, or via your product’s listing on the [Clever Library](https://clever.com/library). Learn more about Clever Library integrations [here](https://dev.clever.com/docs/library-sso).

![Install button found in Clever Library by Teachers](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dhuj&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Djqm9)

Teachers will then be presented with a screen to confirm that they would like to share their profile information to create accounts in your product for themselves and their students. Teachers may also take this opportunity to review your application’s terms of service and privacy policy.

![Teacher view of Allow and Continue page prompted when confirming connection via Clever Library.](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dhuj&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000DjmU2)

After confirming their approval, the teacher will be taken to your product to complete their onboarding and start using your product.  
 

Immediately upon signup, a Single Sign-On (SSO) link to your product will also appear on the Clever Portal for the teacher and all of his or her students. Specifically, the link will appear on the teacher’s [Class Page,](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360001158323?language=en_US) to distinguish it from resources that are managed at the district level.  
 

After signing up, a teacher may log in to their account in your product either through the SSO link on their Clever Portal. Alternatively, if you have a [Log In with Clever](https://dev.clever.com/docs/identity-api#section-log-in-with-clever) button on your site, they can go to your site directly to log in.  
 

* * *

## How "Sign Up with Clever" works for students

Once a teacher has used Sign Up with Clever to create an account for themselves and their students, the teacher’s students may log in either via the SSO link on their teacher’s Class Page, or by going to you site directly and clicking “Log in with Clever”.  
 

In the typical case, students should not need to create their own accounts, as your product should provision student accounts automatically when teachers sign up.  
 

Any new student who joins a teacher’s class will automatically have any SSO links added to their portal, and your application should provision an account for the student the next time they or their teacher logs in.

  
  
 

* * *

title: For Clever Admins: Clever API v3.0
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001448#header1)  
2\. [Features](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001448#header2)  
3\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001448#header3)

## Overview

Announcing API V3.0! Clever’s newest API version simplifies data management for partners and school organization. The next-generation API offers a new flexible data model to help partners meet the fast-evolving and unique needs of their school organization customers in a scalable way.  
  

* * *

## Features

API v3.0 will include the following features:  
 

## Support for multi-role users

In v1.0 and v2.0, users with multiple roles had a Clever ID for each role. This could often be confusing in downstream applications where users might have duplicate accounts or struggle to access the correct account. API v3.0 provides flexible user-role data to streamline the experience of provisioning teachers, staff, and contacts so applications can quickly scale access for all users on their platform. If a user has multiple leadership roles (at the school organization or teacher level), they will now have a single Clever ID.  
 

### What does this mean for school organizations?

This updated data model will not be very noticeable in the Clever Dashboard or Portal. Users with multiple roles will still have separate Portals in Clever. However, downstream applications will now be able to identify users with various roles and link those accounts accordingly. Some applications will also allow users to toggle between accounts.   
 

## Contacts have per-student relationships

We’re adding even more granularity to our contact relationships to make it easier for partners to support and connect with family members. If a contact is a parent to two children, has a nephew in the school organization, and is an emergency contact for a family friend, they’ll have one Clever ID, and you’ll be able to see those unique relationships with every student.   
 

### What does this mean for school organizations?

Contact data will be more accurate and relationship types will be much less rigid. This update recognizes the complexity of the different types of relationships individuals may have as students' contacts. This change will address the security risks of assigning only one relationship type to a contact who may otherwise have other relationship types with other students.   
 

## Changes to staff

API v3.0 will support a consistent experience for how school organizations and applications refer to Staff (formerly ‘School Admins’).  
  
Furthermore, role types for Staff will now be available through the API, making it easy to distinguish between the different levels of permissions Staff have in Clever (e.g., School Tech Lead vs. Portal-Only).  
 

### What does this mean for school organizations?

This update will improve the alignment between how our school organization and application partners communicate about staff users. By updating the way we refer to this user type in the API, we hope to close the loop on some miscommunication that occurs when rostering staff users.   
  
In addition, exposing the staff role field in the Clever API will give application partners more flexibility in provisioning account permissions.  
 

## Content assignment

Some applications allow you to map resources to specific courses, classes, or users. This often requires school organization administrators to work with each application directly to assign these resources manually. To address this pain point, we’ve created a feature that helps you manage content mapping directly from your Clever Dashboard!  
  
To learn more about content assignment, check out this article: [For Clever Admins: Content Mapping.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360052615892)

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**When can we expect to see these changes?**

-   It is up to each application to decide when to adopt the new API version. Even for our early adopters, it will take some time to implement these changes and migrate their data over. If you would like to know more about how an application will utilize our new API, we recommend reaching out to them directly.

  
**How will I know what version of the API the application is on?**

-   You can always reach out to Clever Support for more information about the API version an application uses. However, how each application uses v3.0 will be up to them. Clever doesn't guarantee any specific user experience changes as a result of this new API version release. If you have more specific questions, we recommend reaching out to the application directly.

title: PowerSchool Version 20.11.0
text:
This article is for districts that have updated to PowerSchool version 20.11.0+ and need to update their PowerSchool permissions to grant Clever sync access. 

![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000TVGX&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028DHk) **Please Note:**    
    • **This sync type is no longer available for new setups.** If new to Clever or updating your configuration to pull data from PowerSchool, please reference our article [PowerSchool Plugin Sync.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001590)  
    • If your schools use the North Carolina state-based PowerSchool setup, your sync method is SFTP and the sync is managed by your district. If you are interested, Clever is integrated with NCEdCloud for teacher and student logins! [Click here to learn more.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360026143131)  
    • If your schools use ESchoolPLUS as your SIS, please see our article on [SFTP Syncs](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205783078). This article is intended for districts using PowerSchool as their SIS.  
    • If your district's PowerSchool account has any custom setup, these instructions may not be exactly correct.

* * *

## 

## Updating Permissions

PowerSchool 20.11.0+ requires permissions updates for Clever to sync successfully via DDE. To update your permissions, follow these directions: 

1.  Log in to PowerSchool as an admin  
     
2.  Navigate to: **System > Security > User Access Roles > {click on Role assigned to the Clever access account} > Export/Edit**  
     
3.  Confirm the correct permissions have been granted to the Clever Sync access account to export the following records as outlined in **S****ection 3** of this article: [Setting up your PowerSchool Auto Sync](https://assets.clever.com/website/content/Clever-Sync-Setup-Powerschool.pdf)  
           -  Schools  
           -  Students  
           -  Sections  
           -  Teachers  
           -  CC  
           -  Terms
4.  Depending on your PowerSchool setup, you may also need to adjust your Data Export Manager (DEM) settings. To grant access to Data Export Manager, follow these directions:   
      
    A. Navigate to **System > Security > Users by group** and search for the Clever user account.   
    ![1.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000TVGX&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000002lduH)  
    B. Click on the Clever user account and select the tab **Admin access and roles**  
    C. Under **Roles and Schools**, select the **Action: Edit**  
    ![2.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000TVGX&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000002lduR)  
    D. Check the box for **Data Export Manager Export Access** and click **OK**  
    ![d.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000TVGX&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000002lduW)  
    E. Click **Submit** to save your changes
5.  Once you've made these changes, navigate to the [Clever Dashboard > Data sources > SIS sync > Settings](https://schools.clever.com/sync/settings) page and select **Sync Now.**  
     
6.  Clever will initiate a sync with PowerSchool. To confirm the results, please allow 10-15 minutes for the PowerSchool sync to complete. The sync status will display in your Clever Dashboard.

title: Clever IDM: Entra ID Setup
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#header1)  
2\. [Setup](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#header2)  
      •   [Connect to Entra ID](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#connect-azure)  
      •   [Select your IDM Management Level](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#ManagementLevel)  
      •   [Select Clever users](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#select-users)  
      •   [Data written to Entra ID](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#data-written-to-azure-ad)  
      •   [Data written to a student information system (SIS)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#data-written-sis)  
      •   [Group Membership](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#membership)  
      •   [Summary](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#summary)  
      •   [Preview and provision](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#preview-provision)  
      •   [Events](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#events)  
3\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#faq)

IMPORTANT Moving to the new service principal connection? Edit your existing Entra ID IDM connection on the [IDM page of your Dashboard](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management). Click Disconnect, then [follow the instructions below](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001553#connect-azure) to connect to Entra ID.  **If you don't see the new configuration, please reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326). Failure to do so before June 1, 2026, will result in a failed IDM sync.**

## Overview

Clever IDM helps districts automate account provisioning and lifecycle management for Microsoft Active Directory, Google Workspace, and Entra ID. This affordable new offering provides school districts with a simple workflow that can be completed in minutes to automate account management directly with Clever. Clever IDM automatically syncs users from your SIS to Entra ID, Active Directory, and/or Google daily for an entire year. Your Clever IDM dashboard can be found here.

  
A full overview of the Clever IDM setup process is below. If you haven’t already purchased Clever IDM, you'll be asked to purchase after completing the setup process. More information on pricing and purchasing can be found [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001472).

##   

* * *

## Setup

You can work through setting up your IDM configuration at any time; however, you won’t be able to complete the setup to start provisioning accounts without review from an onboarding specialist or our support team. Our team must review your setup before your first provision to protect your destination accounts and prevent issues with SSO for your end users. Contact your onboarding specialist for configuration review. If you're not sure who to contact, reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326).

 **![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000eAIP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** Click on the following link to find information about [Setting IDM login credentials.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001605)

### **Connect to Entra ID** 

To provision accounts, Clever must be granted access to manage the provisioning of users on your Entra ID domain. The user authorizing the access request must have admin access to the relevant Entra ID instance.

1.  Click **Sign in with Microsoft Entra ID** to authorize the installation of the Clever IDM application in your Entra ID tenant. 
    
2.  Now locate the Clever IDM application within your Entra ID tenant and assign the User Administer role. See [Microsoft support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal?tabs=admin-center#assign-roles-with-tenant-scope) for more information.  
    Note: The Clever Identity Management app is owned by Clever and will not appear under App Registrations. Assign the User Administrator role from the Roles area of Entra:  
    a. In a new tab, search for **roles and administrators** at entra.microsoft.com  
    b. Select **Microsoft Entra roles and administrators**  
    c. Under **All roles** search for **User Administrator**  
    d. Click on **User Administrator**  
    e. Click on **\+ Add assignments**  
    f. Click on **No member selected**  
    g. Search for **Clever Identity Management** and check the box next to the app  
    h. Click **Select**  
    i. Click **Next**  
    j. Enter a justification like: **Enables Clever IDM to manage users**  
    k. Click **Assign**  
    l. Return to Clever
    
3.  Click **Check role assignment.** If this doesn't work at first, try again in 30 seconds.
    
4.  Once the Clever IDM application has successfully been assigned the User Administrator role, click **Next: Select Management Level** to proceed to the next step.
    

 If you run into issues:

1.  Check that your Entra admin user can grant the following permissions:
    
    1.  Read domains
        
    2.  Read all groups
        
    3.  Read all users’ full profiles
        
    4.  Sign in and read user profile
        
2.  Ensure that you have granted the Clever IDM application the User Administrator role. See [Microsoft support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/manage-roles-portal?tabs=admin-center#assign-roles-with-tenant-scope) for more information.
    

If you run into issues authorizing the installation or assigning the User Administrator role, you may see an **Enable Single-tenant App registration** toggle. Toggle the value on and proceed to the optional advanced connection instructions.

![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000eAIP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000esEdF)   
  
Provide the additional information requested to enable installation of a custom app. To locate the additional information, log in at [https://entra.microsoft.com](https://entra.microsoft.com/). Follow the onscreen instructions in your Clever Dashboard to complete the entry. After clicking **Save**_,_ use the step by step instructions above in step 2 to verify that **_your custom app_** has the User Administrator role; use the app name you provided when registering the app to assign the role.

If you are still having trouble connecting, reach out to your onboarding specialist or [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326).

* * *

**Select your IDM Management Level**

Next, choose whether you’d like to set up **Full Provisioning and Password Management** or **Password Management Only**. Both options support Identity Management in Clever—it just depends on what works best for your district’s timing and goals.

**Full Provisioning and Password Management**

This option automates account security and password management through Clever IDM. Since it requires more setup time, many districts choose this path at the beginning of the school year or during a long break. It’s best for:

-   Automatically provisioning, updating, and archiving user accounts
    
-   Configuring password reset, account recovery, and account claiming settings
    
-   Working in tandem with Entra's [dynamic membership groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-dynamic-membership) to write to fields in Entra. 
    

**Password Management Only**

This lighter setup gives you access to Clever’s secure password management tools for matched users, with the flexibility to configure it at your own pace.

It includes the same powerful IDM matching and collision detection as the full setup to ensure the right Clever user is matched to the right destination user—but requires less time to implement. It’s best for:

-   Piloting Clever IDM or starting setup mid-year
    
-   Accessing Clever’s password management tools
    
-   Managing matched users between systems
    

* * *

### **Select Clever users** 

Clever IDM can provision accounts for students, teachers, and staff. You can select for Clever to provision accounts for one or more of the following:

-   **Students** 
    -   Students are users that are enrolled as students in educational courses or sections.  
-   **Teachers**
    -   **Teachers** is the term Clever uses to refer to a district's instructional staff. These are the individuals that are directly managing a classroom and students.
-   **Staff**
    -   **Staff** is the term Clever uses to refer to both non-instructional staff (e.g., secretaries, bus drivers, counselors) and instructional staff that are not directly in charge of a classroom (e.g., school tech leads, instructional coaches, and principals).

These users are often a different employment designation than teachers and may even be managed outside the Student Information System (SIS) in an HR Information System (HRIS)

**Users with multiple user roles**  
If a user is assigned to multiple user roles (i.e., Teacher and Staff) in Clever, they will be provisioned an Entra ID account if either role is selected for Clever IDM provisioning. If the district chooses to provision accounts for both teachers and staff _and_ a user is assigned to both teacher and staff roles in Clever, during Clever IDM setup the district will be able to select the primary role to be referenced.

Additionally, Clever IDM allows you to customize which subsets of users that you would like to provision. If you would like to filter by user type, grade, school, or extension field, please contact Clever Support so that we can make those adjustments for you.

**Graduation rollover date**  
If Clever IDM is set to manage your students, you will be prompted during this step to configure a graduation rollover date. 

![Screenshot of graduation year rollover settings](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000eAIP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl000007WhU2)

If you do not sync student graduation year directly from your SIS, Clever IDM will use this rollover date to calculate a graduation year for use in formulas. To ensure that this calculation associates your data with the correct school year, set a graduation rollover date. Clever IDM calculates the graduation year based on the student’s synced grade level. Data synced before the graduation rollover date will be associated with the previous school year for graduation year calculations. Data synced after the graduation rollover date will be associated with the upcoming school year for graduation year calculations. Providing a graduation rollover date enables Clever IDM to automatically update any information based on the graduation year (OUs, groups, etc.) as grade levels change during rollover. If your expected graduation rollover date changes, you can edit the graduation rollover date anytime by navigating to your **Select Users** step in Clever IDM.

* * *

### **Data written to Entra ID** 

There are two pathways for Clever to set user data in IDM: creation and user modification.   
   
**Creation**  
In the case of user creation, the following fields are synced to Entra ID:

-   User first name
-   User last name
-   User type (student, teacher, staff)
-   UserPrincipalName as configured by the district
-   Primary email address as configured by the district
-   Initial password as configured by the district
-   Any custom fields configured by the district
-   All newly created users are assumed to be unsuspended.

  
**Modification**  
If a user exists in both Clever and Entra ID data, IDM will optionally update the user. When updating a user, the following fields are synced:

-   User first name (if changed)
-   User last name (if changed)
-   Email address (if changed)
-   District-configured custom fields (if changed)
-   Suspension status
    -   Suspended if a user exists in Entra ID, but not in the most recent Clever dataset.
    -   Unsuspended if a user was previously suspended (i.e., not in the Clever dataset), but has been restored in the Clever dataset.

 **![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000eAIP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** If you have questions or comments about the visibility of these attributes or would like additional attributes to be set by IDM, please contact Clever Support.

   
 

* * *

### **Data written to a student information system (SIS)** 

We now provide SFTP access to user emails managed by Clever IDM. The SFTP files can be accessed by enabling Participation Reports, and the associated SFTP server as described in [this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360049642311).  
  
The CSV files in the SFTP server contain mappings of user emails to their Clever ID, SIS ID, and User Type. Districts can use these files to personally build automation for write-back into their SIS on their end. Clever does not support direct SIS write-back automation outside of the above documentation.  
  
 

* * *

### **Group Membership**

Clever IDM can manage users’ memberships in Entra ID, including both security and Microsoft 365 groups. Please note that this doesn't create groups and can't be used to manage dynamic groups. 

  
**Setting up**​To set up group membership management, start by confirming that the groups you want managed in Google are properly configured in the Google Admin Console.

Next, set up [Clever Groups](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001755?language=en_US) to define your membership rules, then match those Clever Groups to the Google groups you want IDM to manage. You can set up one or more membership rules for each user type you provision in IDM. Learn how to create Clever Groups here. Once you have created Clever Groups, learn about IDM group membership management [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001517?language=en_US).   
  

* * *

### **Summary** 

The summary page will display all the selections made for each user type for user account settings.   
Confirm that all boxes for the user types that should be provisioned are marked **completed**.  
  
Click **Preview Entra ID Accounts** once all selections have been confirmed. 

* * *

### **Preview and provision** 

Clever will generate a preview of the number of users that will be created or updated. Additionally, the system will flag any potential issues.  
  
You can also check on specific accounts that will be created/updated to ensure that they follow the process you'd like, via IDM Preview Sync Visualizer. Learn more about [IDM Preview Sync Visualizer here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001528).  
  
The Clever Admin completing the setup guide will receive an email with a CSV summary when the preview is done generating. The CSV preview is also downloadable from the setup guide.

You’ll see a note in your account that IDM Provisioning is disabled and requires review from a Clever specialist. Our team must review your setup before your first provision to protect your destination accounts and prevent issues with SSO for your end users. Please reach out to your onboarding specialist with any questions or for review of your preview before provisioning. If you're not sure who to contact, please reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326).  
  
**Purchase Summary**  
The purchase summary will display the estimated total per year for Clever IDM. Please note this number is subject to change based on the number of user accounts managed and does not include sales tax.   
  
After reviewing the results, select Purchase Clever IDM to proceed to the checkout flow and begin provisioning. More information on purchasing [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001472).

* * *

### **Events**

After your initial Clever IDM sync, you can continue to track changes to your users via the [User management > Clever IDM > Events tab](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management). On this tab, you can select a date range for which you’d like to review Clever IDM creates, updates, archives, and matched users. You can also apply filters to examine changes by destination (if you have multiple configured), event type (create, update, etc.), or specific users by name or SIS ID.

Once you find the event for the user and destination you’d like to review, click the dropdown arrow next to the event to examine more details.

* * *

## FAQs

**How do I add users to groups in Entra ID?**

-   We recommend using Entra ID’s [dynamic group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/enterprise-users/groups-dynamic-membership) functionality to manage group membership. When used in tandem with Clever IDM’s ability to write to any field in Entra ID, dynamic groups offer a simple, powerful way to maintain groups for students and staff. If dynamic groups don’t meet your needs, please contact Clever Support.

**How do I add licenses for new users in Entra ID Active Directory?**

-   Entra ID’s [dynamic group](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/enterprise-users/groups-dynamic-membership) functionality allows you to not only manage group membership but apply [certain licenses to any group members automatically](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/licensing-admin-center). We recommend that you create one dynamic group for each of the different license types you have and use Clever IDM to populate a field in Entra ID to differentiate between the users that should receive those different licenses (e.g., writing “student” or “staff” to the employeeType field). 

**What if I don’t want Clever IDM to manage a user in Entra ID?**

-   We have some functionality that allows you to prevent Clever IDM from archiving users. If you’re interested in that functionality or something else, please contact Clever Support.

**What if I want to manage non-teaching staff with Clever IDM, but they aren't stored in my student information system (SIS)?**

-   There are various options for syncing staff users, including CSV files, custom data, or an Active Directory sync. [Learn more in our article about adding staff to Clever](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/229253547).

**Does Clever IDM automatically calculate Graduation Year for students?**

-   If synced to Clever, IDM will use the **Graduation\_year** field from your SIS. Otherwise, IDM will automatically calculate Graduation Year for students K-12 based on the student **Grade** field. In calculating graduation year, PreKindergarten and TransitionalKindergarten will be treated as grade -1.
-   Students in the following grade levels will NOT have a Graduation Year unless provided by the district: InfantToddler, Preschool, 13, PostGraduate, Ungraded, Other.

**Why do I see a note that my IDM provisioning is disabled?**

To protect your destination accounts and prevent SSO issues, our team must review your IDM setup before your first provisioning. Please reach out to the Clever team if you have any questions or to review your sync before you provision for a new destination.

**I can’t find the functionality I’m looking for. What should I do?**

-   Reach out to Clever Support. The functionality may be available on the back end. If not, we may be able to add new functionality.

* * *

**Related articles:**

[Clever IDM: Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466)  
[Clever IDM: Purchasing & Billing](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001472)  
[Clever IDM: Sync Reports](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001473)  
[Clever IDM: Account links](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001604)

title: Clever & edtech acronyms / glossary
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#header1)  
2\. [Glossary](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#header2)

## Overview

This article is a glossary of terms and acronyms frequently used in edtech. Like much of the tech landscape, edtech has its own set of specific acronyms and terminology. To help you navigate your experience with Clever, please reference the glossary below whenever you encounter an unfamiliar term.  
  
Found an unknown term or acronym that is not covered in this glossary? Please [reach out to Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360001041326) to make a suggestion.

* * *

## Glossary

-   **Account Claim** — [Account Claim](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001695) is a tool for Clever IDM customers to make it easier for end users to set up their Clever, Google, Active Directory, and/or Entra ID accounts. New accounts created by Clever IDM can be accessed by end users by providing two or more points of private information for students and three or more points for adults, all without IT intervention – making onboarding and account distribution easier than ever for time-constrained IT teams.

-   **AD, ADFS**— **Active Directory** or **Active Directory Federation Services** (Microsoft Windows identity service)
    -   Active Directory is a Clever-supported Identity Provider ([IdP](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#IDP))
    -   Support in Clever for Active Directory:
        -   As an Identity Provider: [Single Sign-On (SSO): Log in with ADFS](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202102576), [Clever Badges: How do I enable Badges into Active Directory On-prem managed Windows devices?](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000384086)
        -   With our Identity Management service, [Clever IDM: Active Directory Setup](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001505)
        -   As a source for Staff user accounts: [Staff Setup: Syncing staff with Active Directory](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360028781552)

-   **API** — **Application Programming Interface** - a way for two programs or apps to talk to one another. Programs have APIs so that they can share data easily. Clever syncs with the APIs of many popular Student Information Systems ([SISes](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SIS)). Clever’s application partners sync to Clever’s API.

-   **BTS** — **Back to School** - the time period around the first day of the school year when school organizations are preparing for the return of students for the new school year.

-   **Clever Academy** - Clever's free online training and certification program for educators and admins. You can go directly to Clever Academy here: [https://clever.academy](https://clever.academy/).

-   **Clever Admin** — Also known as a district admin, or [DA](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#DA), this is an individual from your school or school organization who administers your Clever account.

-   **Clever LMS Connect** – A solution that enables application partners to connect directly to school organization Learning Management Systems ([LMS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#LMS)). School organizations can also connect their LMS directly with Clever to simplify application use.

-   **COPPA – Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act –** Federal law protecting children’s online privacy.

-   **Course -** a course is an academic subject. Courses are often assigned a specific course code and title to track academic credit. Examples: Algebra 101, 3rd Grade Science, Concert Band.

-   **CS — Customer Support** or Clever Support - our world-class support team. [Learn more about contacting the Customer Support team here.](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360001041326)

-   **CSV** — **Comma Separated Value** - a file type using text to represent data fields separated by commas with the file extension .csv. CSV files are used in [SFTP](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SFTP) syncs to export data to Clever. CSV files can be opened in programs like Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.  

-   **DA** — **District administrator -** an individual from your school organization who administers your Clever account. Sometimes referred to as a [Clever Admin](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#CleverAdmin).  

-   **ELL** — **English Language Learner**

-   **Entra ID —** (Microsoft Windows identity service)
    -   Entra ID is a Clever-supported Identity Provider ([IdP](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001552#IDP))
        
    -   Support in Clever for Entra ID:
        
        -   As an Identity Provider: [Single Sign-On (SSO): "Log in with Office 365/Entra ID"](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205889768), 
            
        -   With our Identity Management service, Clever IDM: [Clever IDM: Entra ID (Azure) Setup](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001553)
            
        -   SSO to Entra ID: [Setup guide for Clever SSO into Entra ID](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001546)
            

-   **FERPA –** Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA). Federal law that governs the access to educational information.

-   **FRL** — **Free or Reduced Lunch.** May also be referred to as FRP (free or reduced lunch program).

-   **FTP** — **File Transfer Protocol** - The File Transfer Protocol is a standard communication protocol used for the transfer of computer files from a server to a client on a computer network. This is how your [CSV](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#CSV) files get to Clever for an [SFTP](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SFTP) sync.

-   **FTP Client** — [FTP Clients](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/206020358) allow you to transfer files via Secure File Transfer Protocol safely. Examples of FTP Clients would be FileZilla or WinSCP.

-   **GAC** — **Google Admin Console** - The Google Admin console is a central place to manage your Google Workspace services.  
      
    -   Google is a Clever-supported Identity Provider ([IdP](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001552#IDP))
    -   Support in Clever for Google:
        
        -   -   As an Identity Provider: [Single Sign-On (SSO): Log in with Google](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202084503), [Clever Badges: Chromebook login flow](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360024681032)
                
            -   With our Identity Management service, Clever IDM: [Clever IDM: Google Setup](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001467)
                
            -   See [For Clever Admins: Clever & Google](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001659) for additional information
                
-   **Google Classroom roster import** — a rostering [application](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001503) that enables admins with Google Workspace for Education Plus to automatically create classes, populate, and sync rosters directly to Classroom from their Student Information System (SIS) through Clever.

-   **IAM** — Identity and Access Management

-   **IC** — [Infinite Campus](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360049821892), a Student Information System (SIS) used to sync data to Clever.

-   **IDM** — **Identity Management** - [Clever IDM](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466) helps school organizations automate account provisioning and lifecycle management for [Microsoft Active Directory,](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#AD) [Google Workspace](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001541), and [Entra ID](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#entraid). Clever IDM automatically syncs users from a Student Information System ([SIS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SIS)) to Active Directory, Google, or Entra ID daily for an entire year.

-   **IdP** — **Identity Provider** - what school organizations use to **manage identity** at their school organization to allow access to Clever. Many school organizations already have a username and password that students use to access applications on their school site. Common login methods are [Google](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202084503) and Active Directory Federation Services ([ADFS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#AD)).

-   **IEP** — **Individualized Education Program**

-   **Instant Login (IL)** — Instant Login is a way for users to log in once and then access all their connected applications without having to log in again.

-   **Instant Login Link [(ILL)](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205546348)** — A custom link that allows school organizations to embed application login URLs directly into their school organization's single sign-on portal, website, or Learning Management System (LMS). This allows school organization users to access Clever applications via your school organization portal using their Clever credentials.

-   **LEA** — **Local Education Agency**, a public school district, or a public charter school in the United States.

-   **LDAP** — **[Lightweight Directory Access Protocol](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/207090387)** is a protocol for two systems to talk to each other but it is not an identity provider. Clever uses LDAP to match user information from a server (typically, [Active Directory](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#AD)).

-   **LMS** — **Learning Management System** - a software application for the administration, documentation, tracking, reporting, and delivery of electronic educational technology (also called e-learning) education courses or training programs.

-   **LTI — Learning Tools Interoperability** (IMS standard) is an education technology specification developed by the IMS Global Learning Consortium (now known as 1EdTech Consortium). It specifies a method for a learning system to invoke and to communicate with external systems.

-   **Mapping** — The process of linking data fields from one database to another. In Clever, mapping typically means bringing a field from the SIS into a Clever field.

-   **MDM** — **Mobile Device Management -** typically school organizations use a Mobile Device Management (MDM) software (i.e. JAMF, Intune) to add the Clever app to the users' school devices, which allows the school organization to automate, control, and secure administrative policies on their network. 

-   **MDR** — MDR is a company that provisions unique numbers for school organizations. Certain applications require an MDR number for school organizations, such as College Board.

-   **MFA** — **Multi-Factor Authentication** - Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is a way to log in to programs that requires you to use two methods (or factors) to prove your identity, like your username and password on your computer and a text message code sent to your phone. [Clever's Classroom MFA](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001616) (CMFA) helps school organizations protect sensitive student and staff information through secured access to critical applications and systems such as email, Student Information Systems ([SIS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SIS)), and payroll.

-   **MIS — Management Information System** - see SIS/Student Information System. This is the term used for SIS in the United Kingdom.

-   **NCES** — **National Center for Education Statistics** - The National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) is the primary federal entity for collecting and analyzing data related to education in the U.S. and other nations. NCES is located within the U.S. Department of Education and the Institute of Education Sciences. NCES fulfills a Congressional mandate to collect, collate, analyze, and report complete statistics on the condition of American education; conduct and publish reports; and review and report on education activities internationally. NCES provides unique IDs for schools and those IDs can be found here: [https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/schoolsearch/.](https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/schoolsearch/)

-   **NCES ID** – A unique ID value provided by the National Center for Education Statistics for identifying school organizations. May be utilized by some application partners for data tracking purposes.

-   **OAuth** — Shorthand for OAuth2, a standardized protocol used by Clever Instant Login.

-   **Office 365/Entra ID** — [Office 365/Entra ID](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205889768) is a common [IdP](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#IDP) for school organizations using Microsoft products. It's cloud-based, as opposed to [ADFS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#AD), which requires a local computer to run a server. Formerly known as "Azure" or "Azure Active Directory".

-   **OneRoster** — [OneRoster](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115001975103) is the standard specification for securely sharing class rosters and related data between a Student Information System ([SIS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SIS)) and any other system, typically a content application or learning management system ([LMS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#LMS)).

-   **Organizational Unit (OU)** — Organizational "folders" used in Google and Active Directory to group users and devices and often used to apply rules or policies to them.

-   **Personally Identifiable Information (PII)** — Any data that could be used to identify an individual such as their first/last name, email address, sis\_id, etc.

-   **Plugin** — A software add-on that is installed into a program to add additional functionality. For example, Clever offers a plugin for PowerSchool to power the automatic sync of data from PowerSchool.

-   **SAML** — [**Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)**](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/218050687) is a login standard that helps users access applications based on sessions in another context. It’s a single sign-on ([SSO](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SSO)) login method offering more secure authentication (with a better user experience) than usernames and passwords.

-   **Section** — a section refers to different classes or sessions of a [course.](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#course) A course may have multiple sections, each of which may be taught by a different instructor, at different times, or in different locations. Examples: Algebra 101 - Mrs. Bowes - 2nd Period, 3rd Grade Science - Mr. Carter, Concert Band - Harper Middle School.

-   **Secure Sync** — Clever Secure Sync is a bridge between your Student Information System ([SIS](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#SIS)) and online learning applications. Secure Sync maintains up-to-date roster information in your learning applications by securely transferring your roster uploads or connecting directly with your SIS.

-   **SFTP** — **Secure File Transfer Protocol** - a secure file transfer protocol that uses secure shell encryption to provide a high level of security for sending and receiving file transfers.

-   **SIS**— **Student Information System** - a SIS is a web-based platform that helps schools take student data online for easier management.

-   **SIS\_ID** — the unique user identification value provided by your SIS for each user in Clever.

-   **SPMS — Secure Password Management Suite** — a suite of password management tools in Clever IDM that support automated account claiming, password reset and account recovery, password synchronization, and prevention of weak passwords.

-   **SSO** — [single sign-on](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/203166807) - Clever's SSO enables users to securely sign in to connected applications via Clever Portal.

-   **Staff** — Within Clever, non-instructional users are referred to as [**staff**](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/229253547), i.e. principals, office administrators, etc. [Staff members can also have a teacher account](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360032149791) in Clever as well as their staff account.

-   **STL** — **[School Tech Lead](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115003207663)** -  the School Tech Lead role provides a staff member with limited admin permissions in Clever for their associated school(s). This role is assigned by a District or Clever Admin.

-   **Term** — A portion of the academic year associated with [sections](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001552#section) in Clever. Some examples of terms are **Year**, **S1**, and **Q3**, depending on how your schools set up terms such as yearly, by semester, or quarterly.

-   **Users** — Refers to your students, teachers, and staff in Clever (i.e., those using Clever)

-   **User Groups** — Collections of users you create for managing access and policies. Today, Clever supports the management of your Google and Active Directory groups through [Clever IDM](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466).

* * *

title: For App Partners: How do I enable two-factor authentication?
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001551#overview)  
2\. [Setting up two-factor authentication](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001551#setup)  
3\. [Disabling Two-Factor Authentication](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001551#disable)  
4\. [Account recovery](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001551#account_recovery)

##   
Overview

Two-factor authentication adds another level of security to your account. If you enable two-factor authentication, you'll be asked to enter a verification code in addition to your username and password every time you log in to Clever. This extra verification prevents unauthorized parties from accessing your account, even if your password has been compromised.

You can set up two-factor authentication for your Clever account in two ways:

-   Via a text message sent to your phone or device (SMS)
-   Via the authenticator application [Authy](https://www.authy.com/) (available for [iOS](https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/authy/id494168017) and [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.authy.authy))

 **![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cMif&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** Due to the requirement for SSO or 2FA to log in to the Clever apps dashboard, non-human user accounts will no longer be supported.

* * *

##   
  
Setting up two-factor authentication

   
1. Log into your [Clever Account](https://apps.clever.com/)  
  
2\. Click on your name in the upper right-hand corner, and select [**Profile**](https://apps.clever.com/settings)  
  
3. Scroll down to select **Enable TFA**  
  
4\. Select how you’d like to receive verification codes, and then enter your phone number to proceed.   
 

 **![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cMif&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** If you choose to use Authy and have not already downloaded the app, you will be prompted to do so.

  
![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cMif&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BDM)  
  
  
5\. When prompted, either enter your code from Authy or request a code via SMS.  
  
6\. The next time you log in to Clever, you will be prompted to enter your verification code. Enter the verification code received via Authy or SMS. You can ask Clever to **remember** you for 30 days on your device so that you do not need to authenticate every time you log in.   
  
This option is not recommended if you are on a public or shared computer, or don’t have password protection on your personal computer.  
 

* * *

##   
Disabling Two-Factor Authentication

Once you have two-factor authentication enabled, you can disable this setting at any time from your [Clever Profile page](https://apps.clever.com/settings).  
  
You’ll be prompted to enter your current Clever password to disable two-factor authentication.   
  
Please note that you cannot disable two-factor authentication if you have lost access to your two-factor authentication method. If you have lost access to your two-factor authentication due to having a new device, new phone number, or inability to receive an SMS message from Authy, please see the Account Recovery instructions below.  
 

* * *

##   
Account Recovery

If you are unable to access your two-factor authentication code, it will be necessary to complete account recovery as outlined here: [Change the Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) Phone Number Objective](https://help.twilio.com/articles/223136347-Change-the-Two-Factor-Authentication-2FA-Phone-Number-on-your-Twilio-Account).    
   
Clever Support is unable to disable two-factor authentication for your account. The account recovery must be completed by our two-factor service provider, Authy.

title: For Clever Admins: Cybersecurity best practices
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001549#header1)  
2\. [Clever products and features that support your cybersecurity practices](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001549#header2)  
3\. [Cybersecurity recommendations for your school organization](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001549#header3)

## Overview

Cybersecurity and protecting user accounts with access to sensitive information continues to be a key priority for school organizations as more malicious actors target school organizations and exploit vulnerabilities in their IT infrastructure. This article discusses some key cybersecurity best practices when managing your Clever account for school organizations located in the US and Canada.  
  
As always, we recommend evaluating your current cybersecurity practices, environment, and risk tolerance when making decisions for your school regarding authentication and digital identity management. Please also consult the [Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s website](https://www.cisa.gov/) and [their report on cybersecurity](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/cisa-releases-report-k-12-schools-help-address-evolving-cybersecurity-threats). Use this article for general cybersecurity reminders regarding your management of Clever, Clever users, and Clever integrations.  
 

![Clever Academy Logo](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dYhl&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000035fcv)  
If you'd like more in-depth support on school organization cybersecurity, such as creating a cybersecurity blueprint for your school, check out [Quick start - District cybersecurity in Clever Academy](https://clever.academy/quick-start-cybersecurity?user_type=district_admin). We also have teacher training, [Quick start - Cybersecurity basics for teachers](https://clever.academy/quick-start-cybersecurity-teachers?user_type=teacher).

* * *

## Clever products and features that support your cybersecurity practices

Review a summary below of Clever’s various no-cost and paid solutions for supporting your school’s cybersecurity efforts:

### **No-cost security functionality**

-   [Clever Admin multi-factor authentication (MFA)](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202062333): All Clever Admins must set up MFA for admin accounts.
-   [sharing permissions](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/203115007): Configure sharing permissions for your learning applications to ensure that the application only receives data for users who need access to the application. If a user is no longer coming in via your sync, their access to any edtech tool they’ve been shared with is removed.
-   [field access settings](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000501586): Adjust field access settings in addition to sharing permissions to minimize the data you are sharing and ensure that only the required data fields are shared with individual applications.
-   [Clever Portal single sign-on (SSO)](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/203166807): Secure application accounts by providing teachers, students, and staff with one secure set of credentials that they can use to access Clever and any learning application instead of utilizing multiple insecure usernames and passwords.
-   [Access logs](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001698): Utilize Clever’s robust access logs to track user logins, including IP addresses from which Clever is accessed.
-   [Substitute access](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001675): Help teachers securely provide temporary access to select applications on Clever for their short-term substitutes.
-   [Role-based access control (RBAC)](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001702)**:** Admins can granularly manage administrators and staff at scale by giving them the minimum permissions necessary to accomplish their responsibilities on Clever. 

### **Optional paid security solutions**

-   [Classroom MFA](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001616): Ensure your staff, teacher, and student accounts are protected with layers of security with Clever’s Classroom MFA. Use school-friendly second factors like Badges, PIN codes, login pictures, and phone calls to secure accounts.
-   [Clever Identity Management (IDM):](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466)
    -   **Lifecycle management:** Use Clever IDM to ensure your end users gain and lose access to their Google, Active Directory, or Entra ID accounts at the right times. Automatically manage user group membership in Google and Active Directory as well.
    -   **Account claiming:** Help users securely gain access to their new Google, Active Directory, or Entra ID accounts. There is no need to email usernames and passwords or provide a paper list to teachers; use automated account claiming to help end users gain access to their accounts easily via URLs and email notifications.
    -   **Password generation and management:** Use Clever IDM to generate secure, random passwords and phrases for end users based on the criteria you set. Provide delegated and self-serve reset and account recovery capabilities to subgroups of users with built-in complexity settings while Clever prevents usage of passwords found in public data breaches. 

* * *

## Cybersecurity recommendations for your school organization

We recommend you review these recommendations **at least** once a semester to make your schools as secure as possible.  
 

### **Keeping your Clever Admin accounts secure**

IMPORTANT   
Given the unique permissions Clever Admin accounts have, we recommend carefully reviewing these recommendations whenever a new Clever Admin needs to be added or removed from your school organization.

-   All Clever Admin accounts should have [strong, unique passwords](https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/publications/NCSAM_CreatingPasswords_2020.pdf) or passphrases that are not reused on any other service. A Clever Admin can [reset their password](https://schools.clever.com/reset) by following the [instructions here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/202083536).

-   The Clever Admin Owner of your school organization should be assigned to the appropriate staff member. This admin user role has special privileges, including deleting all your data from Clever and creating custom roles for other admins. For a complete list of permissions for the Clever Admin Owner, please [see this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202518038).

-   All Clever Admins must have [multi-factor authentication (MFA)](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202062333) turned on.
    -   If Clever Admins use an Identity Provider (IdP) such as Google to access their accounts, ensure they have MFA turned on via the IdP for access to Clever.

-   Audit and remove any administrative accounts that are no longer in use [here](https://schools.clever.com/team/members).

###   
**Protecting student, teacher, and staff accounts**

-   Certain school organization logins, like Active Directory and Google, also act as IdPs, granting access to additional resources (like Clever). Ensure students, teachers, and staff use strong, unique passwords and passphrases to access their IdP accounts. See [Clever IDM](https://clever.com/products/clever-idm) for ways to ensure that your IdP accounts are always up-to-date and secure.

-   Review access to Clever for anyone no longer in the school organization. Also, review access permissions for those who may have changed roles (i.e., a principal had a staff account but has switched to a teacher role).
    -   We recommend that you implement automated account provisioning for your school organization identity accounts so accounts are managed automatically (so, for instance, staff members who have left your school organization no longer have access to their email accounts). See [Clever IDM](https://clever.com/products/clever-idm) for more information about automated account provisioning for Google, Active Directory, and Entra ID.
    -   You can also automatically add or remove admin accounts in Clever by syncing Clever Admins via SFTP.  
          
          
        

-   Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for teachers and staff to protect access to sensitive services across your organization. Consider implementing MFA for your students, as well.

-   Verify authentication attempts via Clever [Access logs](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001698) regularly to look for any unusual activity (such as suspicious IP addresses or multiple login attempts from an unknown user).  
      
      
    
-   Void and reprint Badges each year during your natural rollover period (i.e., summer or winter break).

###   
**Keeping your sync safe**

-   Ensure that all administrative logins to your SIS, including automated service logins (such as for [Clever-managed Auto-Sync](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/202042973)), use strong, unique passwords or passphrases.

-   If your school organization uses SFTP to sync data to Clever, and you believe your SFTP password was compromised, please reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/) to reset it immediately by clicking **Contact Us** and answering the prompts.

###   
**Protecting other applications**

-   Adding your school organization’s apps to Clever to access with SSO is a more secure way of offering access to users versus creating and maintaining a username and password for each app. Likewise, we recommend you regularly review any apps that are not on Clever and add them if an SSO and/or rostering integration is available.

-   Periodically audit apps you’ve added to Clever to ensure you’re sharing data responsibly:
    -   Review the apps you’ve connected to in Clever, along with the data you’re sharing with them. You can review the data being shared via your sharing permissions, or in the **Application Receives** box for each application.
        -   If your schools no longer use an app listed in your Clever Dashboard, consider disconnecting it from Clever so you’re not sharing data unnecessarily. 
        -   For apps your schools are still using, check your sharing rules to see if you’re sharing data that no longer needs to be shared. For instance, if you were using an app with grades 6-8 last year, but this year it’s only being used by 6th graders, you should update the sharing settings, so _only_ 6th-grade data is being shared.
        -   You should also review the [field access settings](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000501586) for each application to ensure you are only sharing the required fields.

   
Lastly, if you notice anything suspicious with your Clever account, please get in touch with [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/) immediately by clicking **Contact Us** and answering the prompts.

title: Sharing Permissions: Tips & Troubleshooting
text:
This article contains the following: 1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001548#header1) 2. [Sharing rule recommendations](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001548#header3) 3. [Troubleshooting](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001548#header2) 4. [Check to see if a user is shared with the app](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001548#header4) ## Overview This article covers common questions and recommendations for [Share by Rules](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/115000392247).    **![](https://theme.zdassets.com/theme_assets/364037/af574183f2df705f2c75ac31fc7ab01b1a5a3d9a.png) Clever Tip:** To troubleshoot why a student, teacher, or staff member isn't shared with an application, use the [Troubleshoot Sharing](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001477) tool in the Clever Dashboard!    * * * ## Sharing rule recommendations Sharing rules can be tricky! Below are suggestions on how to share / exclude the desired data from being shared with an application To view an example rule in a larger format, right-click on the image and select **Open Image in New Tab**.   

I would like to share...

Example Rule

✓  Teachers

See a tutorial video of Guided sharing: Share by teacher or Standard sharing: Share by teacher.

X  Students

  • Teacher SIS ID > does not equal any of > XXX
OR

✓  Teachers

✓  Sections

N/A. It is not possible to share a section without the associated teachers and students. This request is usually made by accounts that don't want students and parents previewing their class assignments. To remove the ability to view classroom assignments, please see this article.

If sharing by section, it is not possible to exclude a single student from being shared. As a workaround: 
  1. Create a custom section in Clever that does not include the targeted student(s) with the same school, grade level, subject, etc. as the section from the SIS
  2. Exclude the SIS section in the sharing rule

Example custom section:

Custom Share Staff
