3\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001505#header3)

## Overview

Clever IDM helps school organizations automate account provisioning and lifecycle management for Microsoft Active Directory and Google Workspace. This affordable new offering provides school organizations with a simple workflow that can be completed in minutes to automate organizational unit (OU) and account management directly with Clever. Clever IDM automatically syncs users from your SIS to Active Directory or Google daily for an entire year. Your Clever IDM dashboard can be found here.  
  
A full overview of Clever IDM and the setup process can be viewed below:

##   

 

  
_Note: Clever IDM does not yet support home folder provisioning or exchange mailbox provisioning. If you’re interested in this functionality, we’d love to hear from you! Please reach out to Clever Support._

* * *

##   
Setup

You can work through setting up your IDM configuration at any time; however, you won’t be able to complete the setup to start provisioning accounts without review from an onboarding specialist or our support team. Our team must review your setup before your first provision to protect your destination accounts and prevent issues with SSO for your end users. Contact your onboarding specialist for configuration review. If you're not sure who to contact, reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326).

 **![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dc8f&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB)**Click on the following links to find information about:  
• [Setting IDM login credentials](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001605)• [Organizing OUs](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001603)  
• [Building sub-OUs with the IDM format builder](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001603#header3)  

### **Connect to Active Directory**

To provision accounts, Clever needs permission to connect to your Active Directory server. To establish a successful connection with Clever, you will need to provide the following information for your Active Directory server:

-   LDAPS URL (your server’s external IP address or domain name after “ldaps://”)
-   SHA-256 fingerprints of SSL certificates
-   Base Distinguished Name (Base DN)
-   Username and password for a bind account with:
    -   Read/write access to users and organizational units
    -   Replicating directory changes permissions

In addition to providing the information above, if you use a firewall please give access to the [Clever IP addresses listed here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001752) on **port 636** to ensure a successful connection with your server. Also please ensure your firewall reroutes Clever to a domain controller for your Active Directory with **write access**.  
  
For a detailed, step-by-step guide on connecting and troubleshooting your connection to Active Directory, see [Clever IDM: Connecting to Active Directory via LDAPS](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001504).

* * *

**Select your IDM Management Level**

Next, choose whether you’d like to set up **Full Provisioning and Password Management** or **Password Management Only**. Both options support Identity Management in Clever—it just depends on what works best for your school organization's timing and goals.

**Full Provisioning and Password Management**

This option automates account security and password management through Clever IDM. Since it requires more setup time, many school organizations choose this path at the beginning of the school year or during a long break. It’s best for:

-   Automatically provisioning, updating, and archiving user accounts
    
-   Configuring password reset, account recovery, and account claiming settings
    
-   Building and maintaining OUs and groups from your SIS data
    

**Password Management Only**

This lighter setup gives you access to Clever’s secure password management tools for matched users, with the flexibility to configure it at your own pace.

It includes the same powerful IDM matching and collision detection as the full setup to ensure the right Clever user is matched to the right destination user—but requires less time to implement. It’s best for:

-   Piloting Clever IDM or starting setup mid-year
    
-   Accessing Clever’s password management tools
    
-   Managing matched users between systems
    

  
 

* * *

### **Select Clever Users**

Clever IDM can provision accounts for students, teachers, and staff. You may select for Clever to provision accounts for one or more of the following:  
  
**Students**   
Students are users that are enrolled as students in educational courses or sections.   
  
**Teachers**  
"Teachers" is the term Clever uses to refer to a school organization's instructional staff. These are the individuals that are directly managing a classroom and students.  
  
**Staff**  
"Staff" is the term Clever uses to refer to both non-instructional staff (e.g. secretaries, bus drivers, counselors) and instructional staff that are not directly in charge of a classroom (e.g. school tech leads, instructional coaches, and principals). These users are often a different employment designation than teachers and may even be managed outside the Student Information System (SIS) in a HR Information System (HRIS)  
 

**Users with multiple user roles**   
If a user is assigned to multiple user roles (e.g. Teacher and Staff) in Clever, they will be provisioned an Active Directory account if either role is selected for Clever IDM provisioning. If the school organization chooses to provision accounts for both teachers and staff _and_ a user is assigned to both teacher and staff roles in Clever, during Clever IDM setup the school org will be able to select the primary role to be used for OU and group structure.  
  
**Users with existing Active Directory accounts**  
Users with the same email address in Clever and Active Directory will be matched/organized in the OU structure as outlined in step: **Organize Active Directory OUs**. Clever will not update the UserPrincipalNames or sAMAccountNames for existing Active Directory accounts unless a new SIS username is synced for a user.  
  
To ensure accurate matching, please make sure that usernames are synced to Clever from your student information system (SIS) and that the usernames match your UserPrincipalNames in AD. 

Additionally, Clever IDM allows you to customize which subsets of users that you would like to provision. If you would like to filter by user type, grade, school, or extension field please contact Clever Support so that we can make those adjustments for you.

**Graduation rollover date**  
If Clever IDM is set to manage your students, you will be prompted during this step to configure a graduation rollover date. 

![Screenshot of graduation year rollover settings](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dc8f&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl000007WcRA)

If you do not sync student graduation year directly from your SIS, Clever IDM will use this rollover date to calculate a graduation year for use in formulas. To ensure that this calculation associates your data with the correct school year, set a graduation rollover date. Clever IDM calculates the graduation year based on the student’s synced grade level. Data synced before the graduation rollover date will be associated with the previous school year for graduation year calculations. Data synced after the graduation rollover date will be associated with the upcoming school year for graduation year calculations. Providing a graduation rollover date enables Clever IDM to automatically update any information based on the graduation year (OUs, groups, etc.) as grade levels change during rollover. If your expected graduation rollover date changes, you can edit the graduation rollover date anytime by navigating to your **Select Users** step in Clever IDM.

* * *

### **Data** **written to Active Directory**

There are two pathways for Clever to set user data in IDM: creation and user modification.  
 

**Creation**  
In the case of user creation, the following fields are synced to Active Directory:

-   User first name
-   User last name
-   User type (student, teacher, staff)
-   CommonName
-   UserPrincipalName as configured by the school organization
-   sAMAccountName as configured by the school org
-   Primary mail address as configured by the school org
-   Organizational unit as configured by the school org
-   Initial password as configured by the school org

All newly created users are assumed to be unsuspended.  
  
**Modification**  
If a user exists in both Clever and Active Directory data, IDM will update the following fields when changes occur:

-   User first name
-   User last name
-   CommonName
-   Organizational unit as configured by the school organization
-   Optional Custom Fields, such as Department, Title, etc.
-   Suspension status
    -   Suspended if a user exists in Active Directory under a managed OU, but not in the most recent Clever dataset.
    -   Unsuspended if a user was previously suspended (i.e. not in the Clever dataset), but has been restored in the Clever dataset.

IDM will only update UserPrincipalName or sAMAccountName if a new SIS username is synced for a user. IDM will only update the Mail attribute if a new SIS email is synced for a user.  
  
**Additional Mapped Fields**  
If you are mapping additional fields from Clever to Active Directory, Clever will update the AD fields when relevant data in Clever changes. If you decide to stop mapping an additional field to AD, Clever IDM will ignore that field in future syncs, leaving any previously-synced data populated.  
  
If you have questions or comments about the visibility of these attributes or would like additional attributes to be set by IDM, please contact our [support team](mailto:idm@clever.com).  
  
**Data written to a student information system (SIS)**  
We now provide SFTP access to user emails managed by Clever IDM. The SFTP files can be accessed by enabling Participation Reports, and the associated SFTP server as described in [this article](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360049642311?language=en_US).  
  
The CSV files in the SFTP server contain mappings of user emails to their Clever ID, SIS ID, and User Type. School organizations can use these files to personally build automation for write back into their SIS on their end. Clever does not support direct SIS write back automation outside of the above documentation.  
 

If you have questions or comments about the visibility of these attributes or would like additional attributes to be set by IDM, please contact our [support team](mailto:idm@clever.com). 

* * *

### **Manage group membership**

 **![pencil.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dc8f&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** If your school connected to IDM before 8/4/26, refer to [Legacy Groups](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001505#Legacygroups) instead.

This functionality enables Clever IDM to place users in one or more security or distribution groups using formulas. Clever IDM will then manage membership as users’ data changes. For example, if students are placed in school-specific groups, Clever IDM will remove them from their old school’s group and place them in a new one whenever a student changes schools.  
  
Learn more about [AD group membership management here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001517).

  
**Setting up**​To set up group membership management, start by confirming that the groups you want managed in Active Directory are properly configured.

Next, set up [Clever Groups](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001755?language=en_US) to define your membership rules, then match those Clever Groups to the Active Directory groups you want IDM to manage. You can set up one or more membership rules for each user type you provision in IDM. Learn how to create Clever Groups here. Once you have created Clever Groups, learn about IDM group membership management [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001517?language=en_US).   
  

Legacy Groups

**Setting up**  
​In order to set up group membership management, start by confirming that the groups you want managed in Active Directory are properly configured.  
  
All Clever-managed groups must have unique names. As well, if you want to set up a rule to put users into different groups, the relevant group names must follow the same conventions. For example, if you want a rule set up that will add each user to a group for their school, the relevant groups need to be consistently named – e.g. “Toll Gate Elementary - Students”, “Hopewell Valley High School - Students”.  
  
If this isn’t possible for your district, please reach out to let us know. There are some more complicated setups that we can support.  
  
**Membership rules**  
When you reach out to Clever Support to set up group membership management, we’ll ask you for the membership rules you want to create and the groups you’d like Clever IDM to manage. You can set up one or more membership rules for each user type you provision in IDM.

  
  

* * *

### **Summary**

The summary page will display all the selections made for each user type for both user account settings and organizational structure (OUs).   
  
Confirm that all boxes for the user types that should be provisioned are marked ![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dc8f&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BmEL)  
  
Select **Preview Active Directory Accounts** once all selections have been confirmed.   
 

* * *

### **Preview and provision**

Clever will generate a preview of the number of users that will be created or updated. Additionally, the system will flag any potential issues.  
  
You can also check on specific accounts that will be created/updated to ensure that they follow the process you'd like, via IDM Preview Sync Visualizer. Learn more about [IDM Preview Sync Visualizer here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001528).

You’ll see a note in your account that IDM Provisioning is disabled and requires review from a Clever specialist. Our team must review your setup before your first provision to protect your destination accounts and prevent issues with SSO for your end users. Please reach out to your onboarding specialist with any questions or for review of your preview before provisioning. If you're not sure who to contact, please reach out to [Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326).  
  
The Clever Admin completing the setup guide will receive an email with a CSV summary when the preview is done generating. The CSV preview is also downloadable from the setup guide.  
  
**Matching**  
Clever IDM will attempt to match users in one of two ways. First, it will take the user’s Clever username and match it against existing UserPrincipalNames in Active Directory. If a Clever user doesn’t have a username populated, Clever IDM will use the UserPrincipalName defined in the “Set login credentials step” and search for identical UserPrincipalNames in Active Directory.  
  
If there is a match using either of these methods, Clever will match the user (and perform “Update” events, as necessary). If there is no match, Clever will attempt to create the user, resulting in a “Create” event.  
  
**Clever tip:** for the best matching and preview experience, make sure you’re uploading up-to-date usernames to Clever.  
  
**Issues**  
There are a variety of issues that may occur when attempting a first sync. You can view issues by downloading the sync preview files from your dashboard and viewing the issues file.  
  
Many issues result from Clever attempting to create a user using one or more unique fields (sAMAccountName, UserPrincipalName, CommonName, Mail) that already exist on a different account in Active Directory. In most cases, these errors can be resolved by updating usernames in Clever and generating a new preview.  
  
If your usernames are updated and you’re still encountering issues, please reach out to [Clever Support](mailto:idm@clever.com).

* * *

###  **Events**

After your initial Clever IDM sync, you can continue to track changes to your users via the [User management > Clever IDM > Events tab](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management). On this tab, you can select a date range for which you’d like to review Clever IDM creates, updates, archives, and matched users. You can also apply filters to examine changes by destination (if you have multiple configured), event type (create, update, etc.), or specific users by name or SIS ID.

Once you find the event for the user and destination you’d like to review, click the dropdown arrow next to the event to examine more details.

* * *

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**How long does setup typically take?**

-   Set up time depends on the number of students in the school organization, the amount of customization required, and if any errors are encountered with connecting with Active Directory.
    
-   Implementation varies greatly depending on the overall quality of data in Clever, if additional data is required, the Clever Admin’s access to features at the school organization such as firewalls, servers, SIS data, etc.
    

**Can I provision for multiple destinations?**

-   Yes, Clever IDM can be used to provision multiple destinations such as both Google and Active Directory at no additional cost per user.
    

**Does Clever IDM change anything about my SIS to Clever data sync?**

-   No, the sync between your SIS and Clever will remain the same. However, email addresses created by Clever IDM will be stored as part of your Clever data.
    

**What if I want to manage non-teaching staff with Clever IDM, but they aren't stored in my student information system (SIS)?**

-   There are various options for syncing staff users, including CSV files, custom data, or an Active Directory sync. [Learn more in our article about adding staff to Clever](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/229253547).

**Does Clever IDM change anything about existing single sign- on (SSO) access to applications?**

-   No, SSO access will remain the same. It may run more smoothly with the automated provisioning of user accounts.
    

**Can we maintain our current user email addresses?**

-   Yes! Work with your IDM Onboarding Specialist to maintain email addresses.
    

**When formatting the password in the Clever IDM set-up, is this simply to create new passwords, or will this reset passwords across the entire domain?**

-   The password format will only be used for new accounts which are provisioned - this will not reset existing passwords.
    

**Will our email addresses and passwords sync back to our SIS?**

-   No, Clever IDM provides automated syncing only in one direction (from Clever to your destination). You are able to download a CSV file of usernames via the Clever IDM page to upload to your SIS.
    

**Does Clever IDM automatically calculate Graduation Year for students?**

-   If synced to Clever, IDM will use the **Graduation\_year** field from your SIS. Otherwise, IDM will automatically calculate Graduation Year for students K-12 based on the student **Grade** field. In calculating graduation year, PreKindergarten and TransitionalKindergarten will be treated as grade -1.
    
-   Students in the following grade levels will NOT have a Graduation Year unless provided by the school organization: InfantToddler, Preschool, 13, PostGraduate, Ungraded, Other.
    

**Why do I see a note that my IDM provisioning is disabled?**

-   To protect your destination accounts and prevent SSO issues, our team must review your IDM setup before your first provisioning. Please reach out to the Clever team if you have any questions or to review your sync before you provision for a new destination.

**I can’t find the functionality I’m looking for. What should I do?**

-   Reach out to Clever Support. The functionality may be available on the back end. If not, we may be able to add new functionality.
    

**What if my question is not answered here?**

-   Check out our Clever Academy course, Quick Start - Getting started with Clever IDM for [Setup FAQs](https://clever.academy/quick-start-idm/1031502?user_type=district_admin) and [Troubleshooting FAQs](https://clever.academy/quick-start-idm/1031504?user_type=district_admin) or reach out to Clever Support.
    

* * *

**Related articles:**   
[Clever IDM: Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466)  
[Clever IDM: Connecting to Active Directory via LDAPS](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001504?language=en_US)  
[Clever IDM: Active Directory Group Membership Management](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001517)  
[Clever IDM: Formulas](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001555)[](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001604)

title: Clever IDM: Connecting to Active Directory via LDAPS
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#header1)  
2\. [Connection Steps](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#header2)  
3\. [Final Connection Test](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#header3)  
4\. [Common Errors](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#header4)  
5\. [FAQs](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#header5)

## Overview

Clever IDM uses LDAPS to establish a connection with your school organization’s Active Directory instance. LDAPS is different from LDAP and requires different configurations at the firewall and server levels (learn more about the differences [here](https://jumpcloud.com/blog/ldap-vs-ldaps#:~:text=LDAPS%20isn't%20a%20fundamentally,thereby%20protecting%20against%20credential%20theft.)). This article outlines the steps you can take to set up your LDAPS connection and can help you troubleshoot any issues you might encounter during that process.  
  
If you have any questions or feedback, email us at [Clever Support.](mailto:idm@clever.com)  
 

* * *

## Connection Steps

To provision accounts, Clever needs permission to connect to your Active Directory server. To establish a successful connection with Clever, you will need to provide the following information for your Active Directory server:

-   [LDAPS URL](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-the-LDAPS-URL)
-   [SHA-256 fingerprints of AD server’s SSL certificate](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-the-SHA-256)
-   [Username and password for a bind account](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-a-bind-account)
-   [Base Distinguished Name (Base DN)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-the-Base-Distinguished-Name)

In addition to providing the information above, if you use a firewall please give access to the [Clever IP addresses listed here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001752) on **port 636** to ensure a successful connection with your server. Also please ensure your firewall reroutes Clever to a domain controller for your Active Directory with **write access**.  
 

### Providing the LDAPS URL

An LDAPS URL lets Clever know where to look when trying to connect with your Active Directory server. It is a URL that starts with “ldaps://” and ends with your server’s external IP address or domain name.  
   
To provide the LDAPS URL for your server:

1.  Locate your server’s external IP address or domain name. We recommend using your IP address. To find your IP address do one of the following:
    -   Google “What is my IP address?” -or-
    -   Go to the “Server Manager” application on your Windows device and navigate to “All Servers”, where you will see the IP addresses listed for all of your servers.
2.  Copy your server’s IP address.
3.  Paste your server’s IP address into the LDAPS URL input in step 2 of the Connect to Active Directory setup. 

![LDAPS URL highlighted on Connect to Active Directory screen](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dsYP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl000000BrQo)

4.  Click **Test connection**
5.  If the connection to the LDAPS server is successful, click **Next step**.  
    If there is an error connecting to the LDAPS server, please ensure you have:  
    Entered your LDAPS URL following proper formatting (e.g. “ldaps://123.123.123.123” or “ldaps://schoolorganization.org”)  
    Given access through your firewall to [Clever’s IP addresses listed here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001752) over **port 636** and try again. Also please ensure your firewall reroutes Clever to a domain controller for your Active Directory with **write access**.

### Providing the SHA-256 fingerprints of your server’s SSL certificate  
Your server’s SSL certificate establishes a secure, encrypted connection between Clever and your Active Directory server, which keeps your data safe. The fingerprint is a hash of your SSL certificate, which safely stores all of the certificate’s data.

To provide the SHA-256 fingerprints of your server’s SSL certificate:

1.  Click “Add fingerprint” in step 3 of the [Connect to Active Directory](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management/setup/connect) step. If you already have a fingerprint, you'll need to remove it and add a new one.
2.  Clever will automatically download the SHA-256 fingerprints of your server’s SSL certificate. Click “Add fingerprint” once your fingerprints have been downloaded.
3.  You will now see the added fingerprint in the “Certificate fingerprints” table. If you would like to add additional certificate fingerprints, contact Clever Support.

![Screenshot of fingerprint uploaded to Certificate fingerprints table, with red box around it](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dsYP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000004YlWR)

   
 

### Providing a bind account username and password with read and write access  
The bind account username and password are used to request authentication when performing searches on your Active Directory server. Clever needs access to a bind account with **read and write permissions** to successfully provision accounts.

To apply the necessary permissions on your bind account:

1.  Go to the “Active Directory Users and Computers” application on your Windows device and select your server’s top level domain.
2.  Click the “Action” menu then click “Properties”.
3.  Click the “Security” tab in the Properties window.
4.  If you don’t see your bind account user listed in the “Group or user names” menu, click “Add…” If you do see your bind account user listed, skip to step 6.
5.  Type the name of your bind account user and click “OK”. In this case, we have named our bind account “Bind Account”, but yours may be named something else.
6.  You should now see your bind account selected at the top of the “Group or user names” menu.
7.  Click “Advanced” to open the advanced security settings window.
8.  In the “Permission entries” menu, double-click your bind account user.
9.  In the “Permissions” menu, click the checkboxes for your configuration:
    -   Full Provisioning and Password Management
        -   List contents
        -   Read all properties
        -   Write all properties
        -   Read permissions
        -   All validated writes
        -   All extended rights
        -   Create all child objects
        -   Delete all child objects
        -   Delete
    -   Password Management Only
        -   Replicating Directory Changes
        -   Allow for “Descendent User Objects”
            -   Reset Password (allows IDM to actually change the password)
            -   Write pwdLastSet (allows IDM to require a password change on next login)
10.  Change the **Applies to** to be **This object and all descendant objects.**  
      

**NOTE:** Once you have applied the necessary permissions to your bind account, please ensure your server configuration allows Clever’s simple bind authentication method. Learn more about allowing simple bind authentication [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-adts/6a5891b8-928e-4b75-a4a5-0e3b77eaca52).

##   

   
To provide your bind account username and password:

1.  Go to the “Active Directory Users and Computers” application on your Windows device and select your bind account user (this is typically found in the “Users” or “Administrators” OUs).
2.  Click the “Action” menu and select “Properties”
3.  Click the “Account” tab
4.  Write the full expression of the “User logon name” in the “Bind account username” field in step 4 of the [Connect to Active Directory](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management/setup/connect) step. In this case, the Bind account username is “[bind-account@test-ad.clever-idm.com](mailto:bind-account@test-ad.clever-idm.com)”.
5.  Write your bind account password in the “Bind account password” field. Passwords in Active Directory are stored using encrypted hashes and the method of storing passwords will be specific to your server configuration. If you don’t know your bind account password, please contact your network administrator or [read this article](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/kerberos/passwords-technical-overview) to learn more about how passwords are stored in Active Directory.

  
  
 

### Providing the Base Distinguished Name (Base DN)  
  
The Base DN is the starting point when performing a search on your Active Directory server. Clever will use the Base DN to navigate your server’s data.

To provide the Base DN for your server:

1.  Go to the “Active Directory Users and Computers” application on your Windows device and select your server’s top level domain.
2.  Click the “Action” menu and select “Properties”
3.  Click the “Attribute Editor” tab
4.  Scroll down to the “distinguishedName” attribute
5.  Write the “distinguishedName” value in the “Base DN” field in step 5 of the [Connect to Active Directory](https://schools.clever.com/identity-management/setup/connect) step. In this case, the Base DN is “DC=test-ad,DC=clever-idm,DC=com”

**NOTE****:** Your Base DN should be the same domain used in your bind account username, but written in Domain Controller, or “DC”, format. In this case, the domain used in the bind account username was “@test-ad.clever-idm.com” so the DC format for the Base DN would be “DC=test-ad,DC=clever-idm,DC=com”.  
 

* * *

## Final Connection Test

Once you have completed all of the connection steps, you will be asked to run a final connection test to ensure everything is working as expected. If the test is successful, you can save your Active Directory connection configuration and proceed to the next step: Select users. If you encounter an error during the final connection test, the error message will explain what has happened and redirect you to the specific part of the connection step that needs attention.  
 

* * *

## Common Errors

Here are three common errors that might come up when Connecting to Active Directory via LDAPS:

-   [LDAPS URL failing to connect](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#LDAPS-URL-failing)
-   [Bind account authentication was unsuccessful](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Bind-account-authentication)
-   [Could not perform a search with the Base DN](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Could-not-perform-search)
-   [Connection errors during first sync](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Connection-errors)

### LDAPS URL failing to connect

In general, a **Connection unsuccessful** error means that Clever IDM wasn’t able to find an AD server with an SSL certificate at the URL provided. There are a variety of different reasons that can happen.   
  
**1\. Double-check your LDAPS URL.**   
If you use a firewall, make sure that the URL provided is your external URL. If you’re using your hostname, try your public IP address instead. You can find your public address by using a site [like this](https://nordvpn.com/what-is-my-ip/).  
  
**2\. Check your firewall settings**  
Confirm that you have allowed traffic from [Clever’s IP addresses listed here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001752) on **port 636**:  
  
Also, ensure your firewall reroutes Clever to a domain controller for your Active Directory server with **write access**.  
  
Once you’ve confirmed the above, use the test connection button in Clever and monitor your network traffic within your firewall to see if there’s any activity from our IP addresses. If not, revisit the earlier steps to ensure you have the right LDAPS URL and that Clever’s IP addresses are allowed through your firewall over port 636.  
  
Once you’ve confirmed that Clever is making it through your firewall, check the policies you’ve applied to redirect traffic from Clever to the appropriate AD server in your network.  
  
**3\. Confirm your AD server has an SSL certificate**  
If you’ve made it this far, but are still hitting the “connection unsuccessful” error in Clever, it’s possible that your AD server doesn’t have an appropriate SSL certificate. You can learn more about setting up LDAPS and applying an SSL certificate to your server in this article: [Step-by-Step Guide to Setup LDAPS on Windows Server](https://www.miniorange.com/guide-to-setup-ldaps-on-windows-server).  
 

### Bind account authentication was unsuccessful

This error indicates that Clever IDM is unable to log in using the bind account credentials provided.   
  
![Error message stating bind authentication was unsuccessful](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dsYP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000004Ym5W)  
  
The most common causes of this error are: 

1.  The username and password are invalid (meaning that either the username or password were not typed in correctly. To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#To-provide-your-bind).
2.  Your server is not configured to allow Clever’s simple bind account method. To resolve this issue, [read more here.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/active-directory/enable-ldap-signing-in-windows-server)
3.  You have not provided read and write permissions on the bind account. To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-a-bind-account).
4.  The domain used for the bind account username and the Base DN don’t match (with the bind account username using domain format and the Base DN using Domain Controller, or “DC”, format). To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#base-dn-note).

### Could not perform a search with the Base DN

This error indicates that Clever has successfully logged in using the provided bind account credentials, but is not able to perform a search on your server using the provided Base DN.   
  
![Error message for could not perform a search with the Base DN](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dsYP&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000004YlY8)  
The most common causes of this error are: 

1.  Your Base DN was not entered following Domain Controller, or “DC”, format. To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-the-Base-Distinguished-Name).
2.  You have not provided read and write permissions on the bind account. Although the bind account credentials may have been valid, and thus Clever could successfully log into the bind account, a search cannot be performed on the server using the Base DN because read permissions have not been provided. To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-a-bind-account).
3.  The domain used for the bind account username and the Base DN don’t match (with the bind account username using domain format and the Base DN using Domain Controller, or “DC”, format). To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#base-dn-note).

Examples of acceptable Base DNs:

-   DC=testschoolorg,DC=local
-   DC=abc,DC=com
-   DC=clever,DC=k12,DC=com

Common mistakes in this step include:

-   Not including DC=local, DC=org, etc. in the Base DN
-   Including the parent OUs or CN of the BIND account used (these should not be included).

### Connection errors during first sync

The most common connection error that a school organization may see after the connect step is during the first attempted sync. If a sync preview shows very few issues, but the first attempted sync results in many more, it’s likely that IDM’s BIND account doesn’t have appropriate write access. In the issues CSV, these errors could look like:

-   LDAP Result Code 34 “Invalid DN Syntax”: 00000057: LdapErr: DSID-0C090C4D, comment: Error in attribute conversion operation, data 0, v2580
    -   Check that the BIND account has write access. To resolve this issue, [read more here](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001504#Providing-a-bind-account).
-   LDAP Result Code 50 ""Insufficient Access Rights"": 00002098: SecErr: DSID-0315130D, problem 4003 (INSUFF\_ACCESS\_RIGHTS), data 0
    -   This means that the Clever Bind Account does not have the permissions to make the changes it's being directed to. Try these three troubleshooting steps:
        1.  Check that the Clever bind account has the permissions outlined [in this section](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001504#Providing-a-bind-account).  
            Ensure that for all OUs/Users that Clever IDM will manage have inheritable permissions  
            Go into OUs that our IDM users are in and make sure that “Disable Inheritance” is not checked in the settings
        2.  Ensure that your OUs are not set to “protect from accidental deletion”
            -   Please spot check users to see if they’re inheriting permissions. Tip: you can use a powershell script to enable this for all users without having to do it manually.  
        3.  Go into OUs that our IDM users are in and make sure that “protect from accidental deletion” is not checked on the objects tab and ensure that there are no “deny” permissions set as the top level permission in that OU.

* * *

## FAQs

**Why do you use LDAPS instead of LDAP to connect to my AD instance?**

Data sent via LDAPS is encrypted in transit, making it a more secure option than LDAP. Clever considers the data it manages (including the BIND credentials provided by school organizations) to be highly sensitive and, as such, uses the most secure option available for establishing a connection with local Active Directory servers.  
 

**Is Clever’s connection to my Active Directory instance secure?**

Clever IDM uses a bind account to sync with the destination AD server. The school organization gives the bind account the minimum permissions needed -- read/write users + org units (as well as "replicating directory changes" permission to read the latest changes). Clever IDM for AD uses a standard LDAPS package and is limited to these operations: create/update/archive users, create org units.   
  
Clever IDM is not able to make any other changes, such as policy changes or domain configuration changes. Internal employees are not able to view plaintext bind account credentials.   
  
You can read more about Clever’s security practices [here](https://clever.com/trust/security).

* * *

**Related articles:**   
[Clever IDM: Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001466)  
[Clever IDM: Active Directory Setup](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001505)  
[Clever IDM: Purchasing & Billing](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001472)  
[Clever IDM: Sync Reports](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001473)

title: Clever + Google Classroom: Overview
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#Overview)  
2. [Integration](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#IntOverview) [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#Overview)  
2\. [Requirements](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#requirements)  
3\. [Teacher experience](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#teacher_experience)  
4\. [FAQs](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001503#faq)

## Overview

The Google Classroom roster import application allows admins in the U.S. and Canadian school districts with a Google Standard Edition subscription or a [Google Workspace for Education Plus](https://edu.google.com/products/workspace-for-education/education-plus/) subscription for staff and students to automatically create classes, populate, and sync rosters directly to Classroom from their Student Information System (SIS) through Clever Secure Sync. Learn more below about the integration and setup requirements.

##   
Integration Overview

  
**[The Google Classroom roster import application is available to request in the Clever application gallery](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add/google-classroom-rostering)!** 

-   The integration is available at no additional cost to U.S. and Canadian school districts with a Google Standard Edition subscription or a [Google Workspace for Education Plus](https://edu.google.com/products/workspace-for-education/education-plus/) subscription for staff and students.
-   Once the application is connected, and the scheduled sync start date has arrived, **Clever will provision Google Classroom courses based on your district’s SIS + Clever data.**
-   Google Classroom course names will match to Clever section names, and rosters will update automatically as students change sections in your SIS + Clever.

  
The Google Classroom roster import application will:

![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Create Classroom courses and enroll students and teachers based on Clever section data  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Automatically update rosters based on changes in Clever  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Allow teachers to manually add and remove students and co-teachers to Clever-created courses  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Allow teachers to rename Clever-created courses  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Allow teachers to accept or reject Clever-created courses  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Add co-teachers to Clever-created courses  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Allow district admins to customize access dates for teachers and students to ensure students don’t see rosters prematurely

![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRvY)  Allow district admins to bulk archive Google Classroom courses based on the creation date for courses made by Clever.

  
The application will NOT:  
 

![no-entry.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRv5)  Create, modify, or delete _user accounts_  
![no-entry.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRv5)  Modify courses that teachers manually create in Classroom  
![no-entry.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRv5)  Write Classroom grades back to your district’s SIS  
![no-entry.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRv5)  Overwrite any changes that teachers make to their courses  
![no-entry.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BRv5)  Sync Guardian info to Classroom or modify/overwrite any Guardian data

If you are already the district administrator for a Clever account, you can [request Google Classroom Roster Import](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add/google-classroom-rostering) from your [Clever Dashboard > Applications > Add Applications](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add). Districts who do not already use Clever and are interested in Classroom rostering can [create a Clever account](https://www.getclever.com/districtsignup/) here and then request the application.

## Requirements

-   **Districts must have a Google Standard Edition or [Google Workspace for Education Plus](https://edu.google.com/products/workspace-for-education/education-plus/) subscription for staff and students** in order to utilize the Google Classroom roster import application via Clever. If your district has questions about upgrading to Education Plus, please contact [na-k12-gwfe@google.com](mailto:na-k12-gwfe@google.com). 
    -   If you’re interested in finding out about your Google Workspace subscription or for help identifying your Google Workspace Super Admin, please log into your Google admin console.
-   Your district’s [Google Workspace Super Administrator](https://support.google.com/a/answer/2405986) will need to help set up Google Classroom roster import.
    -   For more detailed setup info, see the setup guide [here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001469?language=en_US). 

## Teacher Experience

Teachers will have the option to accept Clever-created courses. They can also decline them and continue managing their rosters manually. Courses created outside Clever will not be modified or deleted by the Clever connection.  
  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BSVl)  
 

## FAQs

**What will the courses be named when they sync to Google Classroom?**

-   Clever-created courses will utilize the section name in Clever as the course name in Google Classroom. You can also customize the course names directly from the Google Classroom roster import settings tab in your Clever Dashboard using fields that already exist in the data you sync to Clever. Teachers can modify this course name if they want, and their changes will not be overwritten by the sync.

**Can we manage when the Google Classroom roster import application will start syncing and creating courses in Classroom?**

-   Yes, during the setup, you can configure your first sync date as well as input access dates for teachers and students separately.

**What time will data sync when you set access dates?**

-   Clever will sync with Google Classroom roster import at 12:30 AM PST/3:30 AM EST on the access date set in the application’s settings.

**How often is the sync from Clever to Google Classroom?**

-   The sync runs on a nightly basis. The sync will also run after each SIS sync and after any changes to sharing permissions.

**Can I pause the sync between Clever and Google Classroom?**

-   Yes! If you need to pause the sync between Clever and Google Classroom, head to [Clever Dashboard > Google Classroom roster import > Settings > Schedule Google Classroom Roster Import Sync Pause](https://schools.clever.com/applications/google-classroom-rostering/settings) and set the pause dates for teachers and students.

**What if some of my district’s teachers want to continue manually managing their Classrooms?**

-   Teachers can decline Clever-created courses and continue manually managing their rosters. Courses created outside Clever will not be modified or deleted by the Clever connection. The Clever team can’t help troubleshoot courses that are manually managed by teachers.

**Do co-teachers sync with the courses?**

-   Yes, co-teachers that you have in the Clever data are synced to Google Classroom roster import. Co-teachers won’t be able to see a course until the primary teacher has accepted the course.

**Can I use sharing rules to control which schools or sections are rostered in Classroom?** 

-   Yes! Clever will provision Classroom courses based on section data that is shared with Google Classroom rostering. You can use sharing rules to prevent certain types of sections from being synced, or to ensure that only the right schools are synced.

**What if the student roster of a Google Classroom course does not match the roster of its section in Clever?**

-   Teachers are able to add and remove students manually without Clever's sync overwriting those changes.   
      
    Google Classroom also has a feature that allows students to unenroll themselves from courses. You can adjust unenrollment settings for Google Classroom so students cannot remove themselves from a class. [Learn more here](https://support.google.com/edu/classroom/answer/11189334).

![Clever Academy.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Srar&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000035fcv)  
Interested in deep-diving into how to best use Clever and Google together? Check out our course, [Clever & Google: Secure Connected Classroom Certification](https://clever.academy/clever-google-cert?user_type=district_admin) available in Clever Academy!

* * *

#### **Related Articles:**

-   [Clever + Google Classroom: Setup Guide](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001469)
-   [Clever + Google Classroom: Requirements & Troubleshooting](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001463)
-   [For Teachers: Clever + Google Classroom](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001470?language=en_US)
-   [Clever + Google Classroom: Semester Rollover](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001492)

title: For Clever Admins: Section Names
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Auto-generated section names](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001501#auto)  
2\. [Custom section names](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001501#custom)

## Auto-generated section names

Section names in Clever are auto-generated to ensure unique names, making it easier for teachers and students to recognize and use them. The auto-generated name is: **"course\_name" - "teacher\_last\_name" - "period"**  
  
If course\_name isn't provided, the section "**name"** provided in your SIS data will be used. If neither course name nor section name are provided, Clever will use **”teacher\_last\_name - period”**  
  
⚠️  Clever can't customize the format of auto-generated section names.   
  
![image.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000TGm9&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000004Y5vF)  
 

* * *

##   
Custom section names

Districts can choose to sync their own section names to Clever. Below are the directions for each sync type. Your sync type can be found on the [Clever Dashboard > Data sources > SIS sync](https://schools.clever.com/sync) page.  
 

### SFTP

1.  Confirm the desired section name is populated in your SIS and exportable. The custom section name must be contained in a **single field**. Other than our default formula, Clever can't combine multiple fields to create a custom section name. 
2.  Contact your SIS manager and request they update your district's sections.csv file to send the field **"name",** with the desired data field from your SIS. 
3.  Contact Clever Support and request we disable auto-generated section names for your district. 

### SFTP (sis-managed) sync:

1.  Confirm the desired section name is populated in your SIS and exportable. The custom section name must be contained in a **single field**. Other than our default formula, Clever can't combine multiple fields to create a custom section name. 
2.  Contact the support team for your SIS provider and request they update your district's sections.csv file to send the field **"name",** with the desired data field from your SIS. 
3.  Contact Clever Support and request we disable auto-generated section names for your district. 

### Clever-managed sync:

1.  Confirm the desired section name is populated in your SIS and exportable. The custom section name must be contained in a **single field**. Other than our default formula, Clever can't combine multiple fields to create a custom section name. 
2.  Contact Clever Support and provide the name of the field as it appears in your SIS. Our team will customize the sync to pull the manual section names.
