title: Clever Portal: Ohio Department of Education - 988 hotline
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001719#header1)  
2\. [How to add the application](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001719#header2)  
3\. [Setting up sharing permissions](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001719#header3)  
4\. [Additional information](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001719#header4)  
5\. [FAQs](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001719#header5)

## Overview

In April 2025, the [Ohio Revised Code (RC) 3313.474](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3313.474) went into effect, requiring schools to make information about the telephone number for the national suicide and crisis lifeline available to students. Specifically, electronic portals administered by the district or schools and accessed by students in grades 9-12 must include the phone number for the national suicide and crisis lifeline, "988."

To support this requirement, **Clever offers a way to add direct access to the national suicide and crisis lifeline website in students’ Clever Portals**. Clever consulted with the Ohio State Department of Education and Workforce on creating this application to support Local Education Agencies (LEAs) as they work to meet the requirements of the law. 

  
 

* * *

## How to add the application

Administrators can add [this application](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add/ohio-suicide-lifeline-support) which links to the [Ohio suicide lifeline 988 website](https://988lifeline.org/) this link to the Ohio suicide lifeline 988 using the same steps to add any other application in Clever:

1\. Log into your Clever Administrator account

2\. Navigate to the [Add Applications](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add) tab.

3\. Search for the Ohio suicide lifeline support, or [paste this link](https://schools.clever.com/applications/add/ohio-suicide-lifeline-support) directly into your browser.

![Screenshot of the Ohio 988 application](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000OVZeo)   
 

* * *

## Setting up sharing permissions

Click **Add Application** to begin the sharing permissions process. Sharing permissions will determine which students/schools will have access to this application. [Ohio law](https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3313.474) requires this information to be shared at a minimum with students in grades 9-12.

  ![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000OVhaj)  **Please note:** While this appears like any other application in Clever, **_no data will be shared in anyway_**. Adding this “application” simply sets up a link to the suicide hotline that a student can access at any point.  

To configure sharing permissions for the application:

1.  If you aren’t already at the sharing permissions page once adding the application, navigate to your [Applications > My Applications page](https://schools.clever.com/applications).
    
2.  Click on the application and then select **Begin setup**.
    
3.  Select **I’d like to customize my sharing**, then select the **Click here to customize your sharing** button.  
      
    ![Customize sharing button](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000ObIhh) 
    
4.  Select **Custom Share by Section**.
    
5.  Configure the rule so that **Section grade** \[equals any of\] 9, 10, 11, 12.  
      
    ![Share by section for grades 9-12](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000OaqLg) 
    
6.  Select **Done editing** and then **Save Sharing Rules.** For any student or teacher associated with a section in grades 9-12, the application will now appear in their Clever Portal. 
    

Click here for a brief tutorial video on setting up Sharing Permissions for the application.

##  

* * *

## Additional information

Clever partnered with the Ohio State Department of Education on the creation of this application to ensure that the information and assets included support districts and schools in meeting the requirements of the law. However, **please note that Clever cannot confirm compliance with the state law on your behalf**.

* * *

## FAQs

**If we don’t want to add another application, is there another way to meet this requirement?**

-   If you don’t wish to add another application, you have a few other options:
    
    -   You can send a Portal Announcement (under the SSO & Portal > Communications tab) to students including information about how to access the suicide and crisis hotline. [Learn more here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360025690932).  
        ![Portal Announcement notification](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000ObMDS) 
        
    -   You can add a “custom link” to your District’s Clever Portal, titled however you like and linking to a URL of your choice. [Learn more here](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205875568).  
        ![Custom section with custom link in the district Portal](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000O7ht&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000ObCCU) 
        
    -   You can add a category to specific schools’ Portal (likely upper schools), which would be done via a School Tech Lead who has permissions to edit the Portal for their specific school(s).
        

**Will any data be shared with Ohio or the “application”?**

-   No, there will be no data shared. The “application” is only structured this way to help you as the administrator scope who it will appear to via Clever.
    

  
 

* * *

**Related articles:**

-   [Sharing Permissions: Overview](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/203115007)
    
-   [For Clever Admins: Customizing Clever Portal](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205875568)
    
-   [](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205875568)[For Clever Admins: Announcements](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360025690932)

title: NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service Migration
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [August 2025 updates about the NWEA to HMH Migration](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#Augupdates)  
          •  [FAQ regarding the pause](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#FAQaugust)  
2\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#header1)  
3\. [Clever migration wizard - districts with both NWEA and HMH today](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#header2)  
4\. [Clever migration wizard - districts with only NWEA today](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#header3)  
5\. [Districts with HMH only](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#header4)  
6\. [Next steps](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#header5)

## August 2025 updates about the NWEA to HMH migration

Some districts that migrated to the new HMH Rostering Service may have experienced challenges rostering NWEA MAP Growth on Clever.

-   **For districts who used the Clever migration wizard and can successfully roster:** You’re all set!  Please roster for NWEA and HMH solutions using the new HMH Rostering Service core app.
    
-   **For all other districts :** Clever is working with HMH to make the legacy NWEA MAP Growth app available again in your Clever Dashboard to meet your immediate rostering needs. Once the NWEA Map Growth app is live, you can use it to roster NWEA MAP Growth as you have in the past.

### **FAQ regarding the pause**

**We already started the migration. What happens now?**

-   HMH has paused the migration, so even if you have made changes in Clever, no further action is needed at this time. Once you see the NWEA MAP Growth app restored in your Clever Dashboard, you can continue using your current setup for MAP Growth, and data will flow as it did before. When HMH is ready to resume the migration, they’ll provide updated guidance and timelines.
    

**When will I see changes made in my Clever Dashboard?  
  
**

-   The HMH team is working through this. If you have questions on the status of your district or school, please contact HMH support: [https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport](https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport)

**Will this impact MAP Growth access for our teachers?  
  
**

-   No, it should not. Since HMH has paused the migration, you’ll continue to access MAP Growth using your existing setup. Nothing changes about how your data is shared at this time. Please contact HMH support if you have questions or concerns: [https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport](https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport)

**Will Clever still support the migration when HMH resumes it?  
  
**

-   Yes. Clever remains committed to supporting the migration when HMH is ready. We’ve developed tools like the migration wizard to make the process easier for districts, and we'll continue to collaborate closely with HMH to ensure clear, timely communication.

**I can’t find the migration wizard in Clever anymore—where did it go?  
  
**

-   Clever removed the migration wizard on July 24 at HMH’s request. Since the migration is paused, the wizard is no longer needed. We’ll bring it back or provide updated tools if the migration resumes in the future.

**Who should I contact with additional questions?**

-   If you have any questions, please reach out to the NWEA and HMH teams:
    
    -   NWEA support: [https://connection.nwea.org/s/support?language=en\_US](https://connection.nwea.org/s/support?language=en_US)
        
    -   HMH support: [https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport](https://support.hmhco.com/s/contactsupport)
        

* * *

## Overview

  ![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000OMZe3)  **Please note:** As of July 24th, HMH is pausing the NWEA MAP Growth migration to the HMH Rostering Service. Districts are no longer required to complete the migration for the 2025 Back to School season. For more information, [please click here](https://www.clever.com/clever-hmh) or see [this section in our article](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001710#Augupdates).

  
HMH is introducing a new rostering application called HMH Rostering Service! On July 15, 2025, the NWEA MAP Growth application and the HMHCore application will be merged into HMH Rostering Service. 

Who’s impacted?

-   Districts with HMH and NWEA 
    
-   Districts with NWEA only 
    
-   Districts with HMH only (no Clever action needed)
    

You can start this upgrade the week of June 23rd or whenever you plan to begin rostering for the new school year. **All districts with NWEA MAP Growth on Clever** will see a migration wizard in your Clever Dashboard starting the week of June 23rd to automatically migrate your data from NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service. Please see [clever.com/clever-hmh](https://www.clever.com/clever-hmh) for more information.  
  

   **![instructor\_c8mlopv788bh4spwj0xrzn2c2\_public\_1712091784\_Lightbulb.1712091783969.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028BpB) Please note:** Be advised that if you have an NWEA MAP growth testing event between now and July 15th we recommend that you hold off on this migration until July 15th or until your summer testing events are over.  If you proceed to migrate while you have summer testing events before the 15th you may lose track of some students, necessitating a call and some work with the HMH technical support team to restore those students. If you are through all of your testing windows for the year, please click continue to migrate your app to the latest version in preparation for the coming school year.

* * *

## Clever migration wizard - districts with both NWEA and HMH today

Beginning the week of June 23rd, 2025, all districts with NWEA MAP Growth on Clever will see the migration wizard pictured below in your Clever Dashboard. The purpose of the migration wizard is to automatically move your data and field access shared with NWEA MAP Growth over to HMH Rostering Service (which is the new name of the HMHCore app).

First, you will see the HMH Rostering Service migration as a task on your Home page. Click **Review migration** to proceed.

![Task for NWEA/HMH migration](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000WjHgc)

Within the wizard, you'll review your sharing rules and field access. The sharing you have currently set for NWEA MAP Growth will transfer to HMH Rostering Service. For districts that already have both HMH and NWEA, the sharing rules will include the sum of all data shared with both apps. **If you are using MAP Growth for summer testing, please hold off on completing the migration wizard until your testing is over or July 15th.**

Please note, HMH already has this data since HMH acquired NWEA; this is just a streamlined way of rostering with no change to who is receiving the data.

The wizard will also migrate the field access previously set for NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service. This transfer will ensure that the fields needed for MAP testing are still being rostered. We recommend **Always share all fields requested by HMH Rostering Service**.

![Screenshot of the migration wizard](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000LzjP7)

If you’d prefer to use the **Customize fields shared with HMH Rostering Service** option, you'll be able to review the special and custom fields you’ve previously shared with NWEA MAP Growth and individually move them over to share with HMH Rostering Service as shown below.

![Review your field access settings screen](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000LzZUd)

Click **Confirm migration** to finish your migration from NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service.

![Migration confirmation screen](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Lzkhl)

You should see this message, and click **Done** to dismiss it.

* * *

## Clever migration wizard - districts with only NWEA today

Beginning the week of June 23, 2025, all districts with NWEA MAP Growth on Clever will see the migration wizard pictured below in your Clever Dashboard. The purpose of the migration wizard is to automatically move your data and field access shared with NWEA MAP Growth over to HMH Rostering Service (which is the new name of the HMHCore app).

First, you will see the HMH Rostering Service migration as a task on your Home page. Click **Review migration** to proceed.

![Task for NWEA/HMH migration](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000WjHgc)

Within the wizard, you'll review your sharing rules and field access. The sharing that you have currently set for NWEA MAP Growth will be transferred to HMH Rostering Service. For districts with NWEA only, the same data shared with NWEA will migrate to HMH Rostering Service. **If you are using MAP Growth for summer testing, please hold off on completing the migration wizard until your testing is over or July 15th.**

Please note, HMH already has this data since HMH acquired NWEA; this is just a streamlined way of rostering with no change to who is receiving the data. The wizard will also migrate the field access previously set for NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service. This will ensure that the fields needed for MAP testing are still being rostered. We recommend **Always share all fields required by HMH Rostering Service**.

![Screenshot of the migration wizard](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000LzjP7)

If you’d prefer to use the **Customize fields shared with HMH Rostering Service** option, you'll be able to review the special and custom fields you’ve previously shared with NWEA MAP Growth and individually move them over to share with HMH Rostering Service as shown below.

![Review your field access settings screen](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000LzZUd)

Click **Confirm migration** to finish your migration from NWEA MAP Growth to HMH Rostering Service.

![Migration confirmation screen](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000Oarx&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Lzkhl)

You should see this message, and click **Done** to dismiss it.

* * *

## Districts with HMH only

Districts that are HMH-only will see a name change (HMHCore will become HMH Rostering Service) and warnings about adding additional data fields. These additional fields are recommendations to unlock future features in your HMH experience. If you don't include this new data, it'll limit your experience on HMH systems but won't break anything.

* * *

## Next steps

Once you have completed the migration wizard, you're all set on the Clever end.

Please review clever.com/clever-hmh for more resources, including our webinar series. You'll see a link to register for upcoming webinars, view recordings of previous webinars, and links to contact Clever Support with any questions about the migration wizard or HMH Support with any questions about the merge or steps within the HMH admin dashboard.

### **Message from HMH:**

We know that some of our customers need to roster for the coming school year before July 15th and that will be fine. However, if you do roster for the coming school year prior to the release of HRS, you must go through the HRS wizard in the HMH platform to gain access to several powerful enhancements by spending just a few minutes in the **rostering service**:

-   **Cleaner user management**: Easily deactivate outdated accounts and ensure your user list is current.
    
-   **Accurate student data**: Confirm that student demographics flow correctly into systems like **NWEA**, ensuring smooth reporting from day one.
    
-   **Admin rostering**: Set up your administrators with the right permissions and access—this is a major new capability.
    
-   **Flexible role switching**: Enable users to seamlessly switch between roles (e.g., teacher and administrator) for a more dynamic experience.
    
-   **Vendor integration**: Ensure your instructional partners receive NWEA results without delay.
    

Taking a few moments now ensures your team is fully equipped to take advantage of these features and start the school year strong.

title: Clever + MAP Accelerator: Setup Guide
text:
This article contains the following: 1. Overview 2. Setup process • Recommended Sharing • Setting up your MAP Accelerator sharing rules - Scenario 1 • Setting up your MAP Accelerator sharing rules - Scenario 2 • Sharing staff 3. Required Fields 4. Support Contacts 

 

 Overview

 This guide walks through how to get set up with MAP Accelerator in Clever. Before reading this guide, please make sure your district is set up with Clever! If your district has not been set up with Clever, you can get started by going to this link: https://clever.com/signup . For more information on setting up Clever for the first time, please see this guide . A personalized learning tool for grades 3-8, MAP Accelerator reduces the manual work of differentiating math instruction by automatically integrating class rosters, MAP® Growth™ scores, and Common Core-aligned Khan Academy content to generate learning pathways—complete with lessons, instructional videos, and practice problems. 

 
 Setup process

 IMPORTANT Before MAP Accelerator will be approved for setup, your district must be using Clever for auto-rostering with the NWEA MAP Growth application. 

 If your district is already on Clever, you can connect the MAP Accelerator application by following these instructions:

 • Log into your Clever Dashboard and select Applications > Add Applications .
• Search for MAP Accelerator .
• You'll then be brought to a page where you can authorize your MAP Accelerator request. 
• You'll be asked if you'd like to request a custom Launch Date. The Launch Date is the first day users can see the MAP Accelerator icons in their Clever Portal. Product access may or may not be available on this day and is determined by the application.
• Once you have made your selections, click Request. 
 
 

 
 Recommended Sharing 

 MAP Accelerator recommends that you S hare by Rules in Clever . Create a sharing rule by following these steps:

 • Subjects:
 • Only the following subjects can be shared with MAP Accelerator: Math, Other, Homeroom/Advisory, and Interventions/Online Learning
 

• Grades:
 • Section grade should be 3-8
• 2nd and 9th grade sections can be rostered, but are not recommended and will produce a warning.
 

• Student data must include the following:
 • Unique email address
• Date of birth
• Grade level
• Students can only be assigned to one class/teacher within Accelerator. If they are enrolled in multiple math sections, only one of those sections can be shared.
 

• Teachers:
 • Unique email address
 

• Sections:
 • Should have unique names to avoid confusion
 

• Staff/Admins:
 • Unique email address
• Only users from the Staff tab can be shared, not District Admins from the Team page.
 

 
 

 
 Setting up your MAP Accelerator sharing rules - Scenario 1 

 Scenario 1: All math classes have the subject listed as math in Clever.

 Clever Tip: How do I know how subjects synced to Clever? Check the Sections tab of the Data Browser . Subject is one of the columns listed. 

 Step 1 : From the MAP Accelerator overview page , click Begin setup . Please note, if you have previously set up sharing rules, you will be able to click Edit sharing . Alternatively, you can set up the sharing rules by clicking Share data now from the Applications > My Applications page. Step 2 : You can select MAP Accelerator’s recommended sharing rules: The sharing rule above will share grade 3-8 math sections. 

 
 Setting up your MAP Accelerator sharing rules - Scenario 2 

 Scenario 2 : Not all sections where math instruction occurs have the subject listed as math in Clever. For example, elementary school students may only be enrolled in one section where all instruction occurs, and that section may have the subject listed as homeroom/advisory or other . Step 1 : If you’ve never set up the sharing rules before, you will be able to customize them from the setup guide (pictured). Alternatively, click Edit sharing from the MAP Accelerator overview page to edit rules you’ve previously set up. Step 2 : You will likely need to set up multiple rules. We recommend Custom share by section because section rules include students and teachers associated with the shared sections. Step 3 : Set up your filters to include only the data you want to share. For example, if your elementary school students are only enrolled in one section where all instruction occurs, and that section has homeroom/advisory listed as the subject, you can include filters for the school, grades, and subject. Click Done editing once you are finished adding filters. Step 4 : Add additional rules to capture different users. For example, your middle school or junior high students may be enrolled in sections where the subject is listed as math . You can create another rule to broaden your sharing to include elementary students where the section’s subject equals homeroom/advisory OR middle school students where the section’s subject equals math. From here, you can again set up a rule with filters to include the new group of users. Step 5: Once you’ve captured the appropriate users, click Save Sharing Rules . 

 
 Sharing staff 

 If you have non-instructional staff (users listed in the Staff tab in your Data browser ) who also need access to MAP Accelerator, they will not be included in a section's sharing rule. You will need to set up an additional rule to capture these users. Click Edit Sharing Rules and Add Another Rule to find the Custom share staff option: We recommend taking a look at your list of staff to determine who will need access rather than sharing all staff. Once you have the list of staff members ready, you can share them by using an identifying factor such as email, ID, or title. As always, don’t forget to click Done editing and Save Sharing Rules before leaving the page!

 
 Required Fields

 Check the Data Quality tab in your Clever dashboard to see whether you’re meeting the required data fields. MAP Accelerator requires the following data fields be sent: Student: name, school, district, sis_id, schools, dob, email, grade Teacher: district, name, school, schools, sis_id, email School Admin: district, schools, name, staff_id, roles, email, title District Admin: district, name.first, name.last, email, title 

 
 Support Contacts

 MAP Accelerator techsupport@nwea.org Clever Support.clever.com (click Contact Us ) Contact Clever with issues that relate to: Setting up sharing rules Syncing required fields to Clever

title: For Clever Admin: Access logs
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/202113063#header1)  
2\. [Features of access logs](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/202113063#header2)  
3\. [How to use Access logs with login error messages from end users](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/202113063#header3)  
4\. [Frequently asked questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/202113063#header4)

## Overview

Access logs give you a holistic snapshot of any attempts to access Clever. Use Access logs to spot any suspicious activity early, to keep your schools’ users and data safe. You can also use Access logs to troubleshoot users who are having trouble accessing Clever.

![Screenshot of Access logs](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000VpL0X)

For example, you might notice that a user’s login keeps getting stuck on an MFA timeout, meaning the user has entered their password correctly, but that they are not completing their MFA security method. That could mean that their password has been compromised, and that they need a reset. 

This article covers each feature of access logs and how you might use them.

* * *

## Features of access logs

**Filter functionality**

You can quickly filter access logs by date, IP Address, status, user, and user type. For instance, if you believe a certain user’s account has been compromised, you can drill down to that user to see their access history. In addition, you can look via reference ID (such as an error code a user has shared with you).

![Screenshot of Access logs filter functionality](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC3z3)    
  

**User access activity**

All users (students, teachers, [short-term substitute teachers](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/000001675), staff, and Clever Admin) access activity shows up as a summary: 

![Screenshot of Access logs user access activity](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000K9cKH)

**Individual access log summary**

If you click the down arrow, you can see useful information, including:

-   the authentication method (e.g. Substitute Badge, MFA, etc.)
-   the final user action
    
-   their user ID
    
-   email address
    
-   error code(s) if relevant
    

![Screenshot of individual access log summary](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC4S5)

Access logs will also include details on Clever Admin and School Tech Lead (STL) impersonations. The authentication method listed will indicate impersonation, and the log summary will contain details such as the impersonation’s start and end time, the user account impersonated into, device details, etc.

![Screenshot of an example of an impersonation event in Access Logs](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Pw6WT)

_An example of an impersonation event in Access logs_

**Emailing CSV exports**

Exports are available only as downloads and will be emailed to the admin who exports them from the Clever Dashboard. You can also email a CSV export by day, which includes all access log data organized by column. If you want to send these exports to a security management solution, you’ll need to send them manually.

![Screenshot of Access logs CSV export](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000IC4qH)

To pull an export:

1.  Click **Export** **CSV**
2.  Select your dates. You can export data for up to seven days at a time, up to 60 days in the past. If you need more than 7 days of data, you can export the data for multiple 7-day timeframes.
3.  Click **Export CSV:**

![Screenshot of Export CSV modal](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000JzEG1)

**CSV exports include:**

-   Timestamp
    
    -   When the event took place
        
-   Authentication\_context\_id
    
    -   This ID relates to a single user’s single login attempt. For instance, if a user logged in with a primary method, requested an MFA code, had an MFA timeout, and then successfully entered an MFA prompt, these would all be under the same Authentication\_context\_id.
        
-   User\_id
    
    -   The user’s Clever ID
        
-   User\_type
    
    -   Teacher, student, staff, or Clever Admin
        
-   Client\_ip
    
    -   The user’s IP address
        
-   Auth\_method
    
    -   Their primary authentication method, such as SIS, Google, or Clever Passwords.
        
-   Second\_factor
    
    -   Their MFA method (such as Mobile app MFA, SMS code, etc.)
        
-   Event
    
    -   Part of the login process, such as:
        
        -   Login\_success
            
            -   Part of the login process was successful (such as a first method, second method, or backup login code). 
                
        -   Login\_failure
            
            -   Part of the login process was unsuccessful.
                
        -   MFA\_prompted
            
            -   The user was prompted to enter an MFA prompt
                
-   Error
    
    -   There was an issue with the login process, such as a duplicate ID, no match to a user in your schools, etc.
        

* * *

## How to use Access logs with login error messages from end users

When students or teachers can’t log in to Clever, they’ll receive an error message that provides information about the error, a copyable Reference ID, possible troubleshooting steps, and instructions to contact their school’s IT support.

![Screenshot of an example error message an end user may receive when their login fails](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000cQ9Z&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000O79S9)

While the login error may suggest steps towards resolution, if you need additional information, please navigate to your  [Clever Dashboard > Access logs](https://schools.clever.com/access-logs) and input the Reference ID for more details.

If you’re still unsure how to resolve the issue, please [contact Clever Support](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360001041326) and provide the user’s Clever ID and the Reference ID so our team can help troubleshoot further. 

* * *

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)

-   **What’s the length of logging shown in Clever?** 
    
    -   Five days.
        

-   **What’s the length of logging shown from the CSV download?**
    
    -   You can download up to seven days of data from the past 60 days.  
          
        

-   **What does it mean if an authentication method is “Impersonation?”**
    
    -   This means that a Clever Admin impersonated a teacher or student account, or if this setting is enabled for your school, an STL impersonated into a teacher account. Click the Access log entry for more details on the impersonation.
        

-   **What fields can you search via?**
    
    -   As of now, you can only search via reference ID.
        

-   **What errors might we see in a log?**
    
    -   Wrong email, wrong pw, incorrect 2nd factor
        
    -   Pending MFA: users have 10 minutes to complete their MFA challenge, if nothing happens, Clever will fail the login. 
        
    -   Timeout error: Meaning it took longer than 15 seconds for Clever to download your data.
        

-   **What are the differences between our classic login logs versus new access logs?**
    
    -   Length of logs shown:
        
        -   2,000 logs or 14 days in login logs
            
        -   5 days for access logs with no limit on # of logs
            
    -   Download limits:
        
        -   5k logs for login logs
            
        -   14 days with access logs (you can also request a longer history by contacting Clever Support).
            
    -   Access logs also include:
        
        -   Combined logs into one view when there are multiple access touch points, so it’s easier to troubleshoot.
            
        -   More detail around methods of authentication, such as MFA, Substitute Badge access, etc.
            
        -   Better error messaging with more detail on access errors.

title: Clever Portal: Hiding applications and disabling logins
text:
This article contains the following: 1. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360045814792#one) 2\. [Hiding apps vs disabling logins](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360045814792#hidingdisabling) 3\. [Hiding SSO or SSO (Saved Password) applications](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360045814792#sso) 4\. [How Clever Admins and School Tech Leads hide resources in the Clever Portal](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360045814792#linked) 5\. [How do hidden applications appear in Clever Portal](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360045814792#three) ## Overview This article is an overview of the various methods for preventing logins and hiding applications in Clever. A school organization may wish to hide applications in a Clever Portal for many reasons, from scheduling an application launch to hiding resources during testing periods. Clever's visibility settings allow schools to manage application access with ease.  * * * ## Hiding apps vs disabling logins There are several options for Clever Admins and teachers to hide or limit access to applications through Clever.  If you want to: - Allow logins to Clever and the application, but hide the application in the Portal, you'll want to use settings for **Hiding in Portal.** - Allow logins to Clever, but disable logins to the application and hide it in the Portal, use **App Visibility**. - Prevent logins to Clever and to applications via Clever use **Access Control.** To better understand this, we have created a table that provides insight into these options. Please note that none of the features listed in the table below will block direct access to apps rostered through Clever (e.g. users can still log into the app at the app's website outside of Clever if the application supports this).

Feature

Access Control

 

App Visibility Settings

Hiding in Portal

Teacher Page Category Hiding

About the feature

Clever Admins can temporarily block Clever Portal access so that users can’t access Clever and their applications through Clever.

Clever Admins can hide specific applications in Clever and prevent users from using Log in with Clever (LIWC) buttons. The app will show up as disabled on Teacher Pages.

Clever Admins and School Tech Leads (if enabled) can hide specific apps and links on the District Page, but applications that are on Teacher Pages are still visible and can be used.

Teachers can enable this to hide categories and resources within the category on a Teacher Page.  This doesn’t affect visibility outside of the specific category on that Teacher Page.

Who can configure

Clever Admins

Clever Admins

Clever Admins/School Tech Leads (STLs)

Teachers

Staff/Teacher/Student Portal Experience

Specified user types can't log into Clever or use Login with Clever (LIWC) buttons

Specified user types can't log into Specific App or use LIWC buttons to access Specific App

Specified user types can't see the app in the Portal resource list or District Page (but can still see, use, and add on Teacher Pages)

Students will not be able to see the hidden category on a Teacher Page

Is the app visible in the Clever Portal?

No - there is no access to the Portal

No - the app isn't visible in Portal and shows up as disabled in Teacher Pages

Yes

Can it be set for specific dates?

Yes

Yes

Which users can this be applied to?

Staff, Teachers, Students - set by user type

Staff, Teachers, Students - set by user type

Does it hide the app everywhere?

Yes - no access to the Portal

Help Center Articles

Temporarily disable Clever logins using Access Control

Clever Portal: Hiding Applications
Clever Portal: Disable logins to applications

Clever Portal: Hiding Applications

Clever Portal: Teacher Pages

Recommended Uses

Block user access during pre-school-year rollover to prevent early visibility of schedules/assignments

Block Clever-powered access to apps

  • For links
  • Usable by STLs
  • When you want teachers to be able to add apps to Teacher Pages but don't want an app visible on general Portal 

For teachers to hide resources they aren't currently using on their Teacher Pages

## Hiding SSO or SSO (Saved Passwords) applications **Step 1:** Log in to the Clever Dashboard and navigate to [Clever Dashboard > Applications > My applications](https://schools.clever.com/applications) and click the app you'd like to hide. This will disable the application for the selected users. **Step 2:** Go to the Settings tab and click **Edit** in the Application’s visibility box. ![HC\_artilces\_-\_Google\_Slides-9.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BMAh) **Step 3:** Select the user type you wish to hide the application from. Step 5 outlines hiding from multiple user types. ![HC\_artilces\_-\_Google\_Slides-10.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BMB6) **Step 4:** Select the Start and End Dates for hiding the application.  If you aren’t sure when you’d like to unhide the application, you can leave that field blank to keep the application hidden until you set a date or unhide it. ### ![HC\_artilces\_-\_Google\_Slides-11.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BMBL) **Step 5:** To hide the application from an additional user type, just click **Hide** and set the dates for that user type.  ### ![HC\_artilces\_-\_Google\_Slides-12.png](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P000003BMBa) ### **How do I change when an application will be disabled?** You can return to the application visibility options to edit Start and End Dates at any time. You can also immediately unhide an application by clicking **Visible** next to the relevant user type. * * * ## How Clever Admins and School Tech Leads hide resources in the Clever Portal ![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028CIS)**Please note:** Applications must be put into a category before they can be hidden. For more detailed instructions please read: [How do I manage the Clever Portal?](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/205875568) Clever Admins, and if enabled, School Tech Leads, can hide applications directly via Portal settings. Hiding an application via Portal settings will hide the application in the District Resources section of the Portal, but if the teacher has favorited the app or added it to a Teacher Page, it won’t be hidden. Similarly, if a student or staff member has favorited the app, it won’t be hidden. When hiding an application in the Portal, you’ll also have the option to set different hidden dates per user type. For example, you can hide an application from teachers from June 20th to August 1st, but hide it from students June 20th to August 15th. This can be helpful when rolling out a new application. To hide an application: 1. Navigate to your [Clever Dashboard > Portal > Organize district portal page.](https://schools.clever.com/portal/customize) 2. Locate the application you wish to hide and click the three vertical dots. 3. Select **Hide/show in Portal.** 4. Select **Hide temporarily**. 5. Select all users (student, teachers, staff) you want to hide the application from for the same timeframe. If you want to hide the application for a separate user type for a different timeframe, you can use the **Add another user type** button after you configure the timeframe for your first user type. 6. Fill in the start and end dates for hiding. 7. Click **Save.** 8. Be sure to select **Publish changes** in the top right corner of the Organize district portal page to apply the visibility settings. ## How do hidden applications appear in Clever Portal? When hiding is enabled, the application icon will display on the [Clever Dashboard > Portal > Organize district portal page](https://schools.clever.com/portal/customize) was grayed out to indicate it's hidden from users. If you hover over the app, it'll display a tool tip to let you know hiding is enabled. In the user's Clever Portal, the application icon will be _fully_ hidden until the End Date is reached. ![A side-by-side comparison of a visible/hidden application](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000dKen&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000XPFLr) _A side-by-side comparison of a visible/hidden application._ * * * **Related articles:** - [Temporarily disable Clever logins using Access Control](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360046702972)[](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360000311483) - [Clever Portal: Teacher Pages](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/360001158323#organizing_teacher_pages)

title: For Families: What is Clever?
text:
This article contains the following:  
1\. [What is Clever?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360043488892#h_3dd15e08-a7b2-473c-9586-07b90362d1e9)  
2. [How can my child log in to Clever?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360043488892#h_ef3087d0-82ed-42d4-8ad9-66078b10f141)  
3\. [What should I do if I have a problem with Clever or a learning program?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360043488892#h_f708f1c1-3e02-44b8-be91-47bebe88424b)  
4\. [Is Clever safe for my child to use?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/360043488892#h_ab5dbcb4-dd21-4dad-ab09-1e687aa06717)

##   
What is Clever?

Clever is an easy way for your child to log in and learn with all of the online programs they use at school. With their own personal portals, students can learn with resources selected by their teacher and district.

Schools use Clever so students can have all of their digital resources in one place. Clever also eliminates the need to remember multiple usernames and passwords.

* * *

##   
How can my child log in to Clever?

Your student can visit [clever.com/login](https://clever.com/login) to find their school and log in to Clever with their school-provided username and password. If your child has a Clever Badge, they can use their Badge to sign in at clever.com/badges.

Your school district may create a parent/guardian account that you can use to help your child log in. Learn more about parent/guardian accounts.

##   

 

* * *

##   
What should I do if I have a problem with Clever or a learning program?

If your child is unable to log in to Clever or if you encounter a problem with one of the programs on Clever, please contact your school. Your school will be able to help your child access their account, and can help troubleshoot any issues you may have run into.

Similarly, if you'd like more information on the applications and tools your child has access to, or believe they should have access to additional learning materials, please contact your school directly. The Clever team can't assist with student access to learning materials as your school manages this.

* * *

##   
Is Clever safe for my child to use?

Clever has worked with school districts and learning applications to create a safe, secure, private, experience for every student. Clever is set up and managed by schools - so every resource your child sees on Clever has been selected by their school. The data in Clever is only used to support your child’s education - it is never sold or used for advertising. 

Detailed information about Clever’s privacy, security and compliance policies and practices can be found in the [Trust Center](https://clever.com/trust).

title: For Clever Admins: iOS devices & the Clever app
text:
This article contains the following:  
1. [Overview](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#overview)  
2. [How do I add the Clever iOS app?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#add)  
3. [Expected Login Behavior](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#Header1)  
4. [What happens when a user selects a learning application?](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#select-app)  
5. [Best practices for using multiple apps in one session](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#switch)  
6. [Best practices for logging out of Clever](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#Header4)  
7\. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#FAQs)

##   
Overview

Students can log in to Clever on iPads using the Clever Single sign-on (SSO) application. The application allows students to access the Clever Portal and their Teacher Pages directly in the application, rather than launching Clever in a web browser. This article outlines the process of adding the app and its functionality for students.

  **![pencil](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bfDt&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EMPl00000Zg81p)  Please note:** The Clever iOS application doesn't support teacher, staff, or administrator logins. These users should access Clever via a web browser on their iOS device.

* * *

## How do I add the Clever iOS app?

The Clever application is available for free via the [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clever-instant-login/id1134186971). You can add the application to your devices manually, or use the Apple School Manager (ASM) and your MDM solution to find the Clever application and install it wirelessly to your iOS devices. Please see [more information below](https://support.clever.com/s/articles/115003629943#janupdate) on updating versions.

The Clever iOS app requires iOS 16.6 or later and is compatible with iPhones and iPads.

If you are using older devices that don’t support iOS 16.6+, your users can still access Clever via a web browser on their iOS device by opening the browser and navigating to your school organization’s Portal URL (found on your [Clever Dashboard > Portal > Portal settings page](https://schools.clever.com/portal/settings/url)). From the browser, students can continue to log in to their Portal with their Badge or login credentials.

* * *

## Expected Login Behavior

  
**Students logging in with Badges**

1.  Please be sure your devices have the [Clever iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clever/id1134186971) from the Apple App Store.
    
2.  Users will click on the Clever app to open it.
    
3.  The first screen students will see is the Clever Badge camera.
    
4.  Students have the ability to toggle between the front-facing and back-facing cameras.
    
5.  Students will need to hold their badge up to the camera on the mobile device.
    
6.  If the student is using a valid badge, they will see a green checkmark with sparkles signifying a successful login!
    
    -   _If the student sees a badging error message, they may need to reach out to their teacher or a Clever Admin for assistance._
        

7.  The student will then be logged into the Clever application and their Clever Portal. They can access all features of their Clever Portal, including their Teacher Pages, directly in the Clever app.
    
8.  Please see our section below on what happens when a user selects a learning application to learn more about the user experience beyond logging in.
    

You can preview the student experience in our videos below:

##   

An example of what the login could look like for students using a Badge and [Classroom MFA](https://support.clever.com/hc/s/articles/000001616) pictures.

##   

**Logging in with credentials**

1.  Please be sure your devices have the Clever iOS app from the [Apple App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/clever/id1134186971).
    
2.  When opening the Clever app, users will see the Badge Camera.
    
3.  They’ll select the “Password” tab at the bottom of the screen.
    
4.  The user will locate their school from the Clever login page.
    
5.  They’ll then select the method they want to use to login (ex: Login with Google or Login with Clever).
    
6.  The user will type their credentials and then be logged into the Clever application and their Clever Portal. They can access all features of their Clever Portal, including their Teacher Pages, directly in the Clever app.
    
7.  Please see our section below on what happens when a user selects a learning application to learn more about the user experience beyond logging in.
    

## 

![](/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Pl000000bfDt&feoid=00N1P00000A2RcS&refid=0EM1P0000028Cl0)**Please note:** The Clever app will remember the user's school organization after their first login on the device, so this user won't need to go through the process of selecting their school again if the Safari browser and/or Clever app were never fully closed, and device history has not been deleted.

* * *

## What happens when a user selects a learning application?

After users sign into the Clever app and they select an application, they'll be automatically authenticated into that learning application either in your device’s default web browser or the app’s standalone iOS application.

The login functionality is determined by application partners on a per-app basis.
